proposedTags.rationale: Several cards OVERRIDE the base skill used for a test with a fixed number, rather than swapping which skill is used (BuffStatsReplace) or adding a modifier (StatsModBoostInTest). Duke (02014): 'Fight. You attack with a base [combat] skill of 4'; 'Investigate. You investigate with a base [intellect] skill of 4.' Strange Solution (02263): 'Attack with a base [combat] skill of 6.' Strange Solution (02264): 'Evade with a base [agility] skill of 6.' Red-Gloved Man (02310): 'raise the base value of each of those skills to 6.' No existing tag expresses 'sets base stat to N'; BuffStatsReplace only handles stat-for-stat swaps and StatsModBoost only handles +N modifiers. The fixed base value is the searchable thing (these are deterministic, chaos-token-vulnerable attackers/investigators).

Exile is a NEW mechanic introduced in this very pack (dwl) — a card removed from the game on use, affecting campaign/deckbuilding (must be re-purchased with XP). It is searched as its own deckbuilding cost/keyword. Fire Extinguisher (02114): 'Exile Fire Extinguisher: Evade...'; Flare (02115): 'Exile Flare' on both modes; Stroke of Luck (02271): 'you may choose to exile Stroke of Luck. If you do, this test is automatically successful.' The old regex emitted 'exile' but no taxonomy tag exists. Distinct from DiscardFromPlaySelf (goes to discard, recoverable) and rfg_self/RemoveFromGame which the digest also lacks.

Putting a card directly INTO play (bypassing the normal play action / sometimes ignoring cost) is unrepresented. PlayArea only covers leaving play (to-hand/to-deck); recursion only returns cards to hand. Flare (02115): 'Search the top 9 cards of any investigator's deck for an [[Ally]] asset and put it into play under your control.' A Chance Encounter (02270): 'Choose an [[Ally]] asset in any player's discard pile. Put that asset into play under your control.' Joey 'The Rat' Vigil (02265): 'Choose an [[Item]] asset from your hand and play it (paying its cost).' This 'cheat into play / play from elsewhere' is a distinct deckbuilding capability players search for; the source (deck/discard/hand) is the meaningful variant.

proposedTags.suggestedName: TagTypeDamage.DamageRedirectAttack (redirect an enemy attack's damage to another enemy)
proposedTags.rationale: Reassigning an attacking enemy's damage onto a DIFFERENT enemy is unrepresented. The digest has DamageInsteadRange (your-attack-misses redirection by margin) but nothing for 'take this enemy attack's damage and deal it to another enemy.' Oops! (02113): 'Deal this attack's damage to a different enemy at your location.' Aquinnah (02308): 'Deal that enemy's damage to any enemy at your location, instead.' Old regex used redirect_damage with enemy_value_damage but the redirect itself has no tag. This is a recognizable 'redirect/turn-attacks-on-enemies' combat archetype.

Giving or trading assets/resources between investigators is unrepresented. Teamwork (02018): 'Investigators at your location may give or trade any number of [[Item]] assets, [[Ally]] assets, or resources among one another.' Old regex emitted transfer_asset / transfer_resource but no taxonomy tag exists. This is a multiplayer-support archetype (pooling gear/economy) distinct from gain-resource (which creates new resources) and to-hand/recursion.

Granting the controller EXTRA actions is unrepresented. ActionAdditional in the digest is about a card's ability costing/granting an action restricted to a use (canOnlyBeUsedTo), not 'gain N free actions this turn.' Ace in the Hole (02266): 'You may take an additional 3 actions this turn.' Quick Thinking (02229): 'you may immediately take an action as if it were your turn (this action does not count toward the number of actions you can take each turn).' This action-economy burst is a high-value searchable archetype. (If ActionAdditional.value is intended to cover this, that should be documented; the doc comment 'Assume 1 action if not specified' suggests it is about action-cost, not action-grant.)

Increasing maximum hand size is unrepresented; the only hand-related items in the digest are TagTypeCostAction.CostActionDiscardFromHand and the upkeep CheckHandSize timing point. Laboratory Assistant (02020): 'Your maximum hand size is increased by 2.' This is a small but distinct enabler for hand-size-matters cards (e.g. Higher Education's 'while you have 5 or more cards in your hand'), worth tagging for that synergy package.

proposedTags.suggestedName: TagTypeDeckManipulate.DeckLookTop / DeckReorderTop (look at top card and place on bottom / reorder)
proposedTags.rationale: Looking at the top card of a deck and reordering it (scry / encounter-deck control) is unrepresented. DeckSearch is for digging N cards for a target; this is non-search peeking/reordering. Alyssa Graham (02232): 'Look at the top card of either the encounter deck or any player deck. You may then add 1 doom... to place the looked-at card on the bottom of its deck.' Dr. William T. Maleson (02302) is adjacent (cancels an encounter draw and reshuffles). Old regex emitted look_at_encounter / look_at_investigator / order_encounter / bottom_of_deck with no taxonomy home. Encounter-deck-smoothing is a recognizable control archetype.

proposedCompoundTags.conceptDescription: Cards that exile themselves (remove from game) when used — a deckbuilding/campaign-economy archetype unique to the Dunwich cycle that players intentionally seek or avoid when building XP-limited decks.
proposedCompoundTags.rationale: Exile is introduced in this pack and recurs across cycles (Fire Extinguisher, Flare, Stroke of Luck here; later Time Warp, Eucatastrophe, etc.). Grouping the exile keyword lets a deckbuilder find all 'one powerful use, then gone' cards. Quoting Fire Extinguisher (02114) 'Exile Fire Extinguisher' and Stroke of Luck (02271) 'exile Stroke of Luck'.

proposedCompoundTags.conceptDescription: Cards that grant the controller extra/immediate actions or otherwise increase action throughput — a burst-tempo archetype players search together.
proposedCompoundTags.rationale: Ace in the Hole (02266) 'take an additional 3 actions this turn' and Quick Thinking (02229) 'immediately take an action as if it were your turn' are the same searchable archetype (extra-action tempo). Worth naming now so later extra-action cards (e.g. The Painted World, Momentum) group here.

proposedCompoundTags.conceptDescription: Cards that turn an enemy's own attack damage against another enemy, or otherwise redirect attack damage onto enemies — a defensive-into-offensive control package.
proposedCompoundTags.rationale: Oops! (02113) 'Deal this attack's damage to a different enemy at your location' and Aquinnah (02308) 'Deal that enemy's damage to any enemy at your location, instead' share the 'use enemy power against enemies' archetype that deck-builders look for as tank/control tech.

proposedCompoundTags.conceptDescription: Cards that put other cards directly into play from deck, discard, or hand (bypassing the normal play action / sometimes ignoring cost) — a tempo/recursion archetype distinct from drawing or searching to hand.
proposedCompoundTags.rationale: Flare (02115) 'put it into play under your control', A Chance Encounter (02270) 'Put that asset into play under your control', and Joey 'The Rat' Vigil (02265) 'play it (paying its cost)' all cheat assets into play. A unifying compound lets players find this whole 'put into play' enabler family across sources.

archetypes.name: Chaos-token reaction payoff
archetypes.description: Cards that trigger off (or punish) specific symbol tokens being revealed during a test — already well-served by existing chaos-reveal/ignore tags, but this pack establishes the dense web of 'symbol revealed -> bonus' payoffs.

archetypes.name: Big-damage firearms (ammo weapons)
archetypes.description: High-combat-boost, +damage attack assets gated by ammo uses — the Guardian firearm package.

archetypes.name: Willpower-attack spells (charges + chaos drawback)
archetypes.description: Mystic 'Fight using willpower instead of combat' charge assets with a chaos-token horror/end-turn downside.

archetypes.name: Resource economy / big money
archetypes.description: Cards that generate resources, reward having zero resources, or convert spent resources into stats — a recognizable economy package.

archetypes.name: Resign / scenario-exit and campaign growth
archetypes.description: Permanents and events tied to campaign progression, victory display, and resigning.

coverageNotes:
Analyzed all 76 player cards in dwl. The EXISTING taxonomy already covers the large majority of effects well, so the true gap is small: stat boosts (boost-in-test / boost-passive / pump / stat-from-spent-resource), uses (ammo/charge/supply starting + spend costs), bold actions (fight/evade/investigate/parley/resign), damage-plus, heal damage/horror with you/investigator/ally/soak targeting, discover-clue + additional-clue families, the full chaos-token reveal/ignore/seal/cancel families (Defiance, Lucky Dice, Ritual Candles, Jewel of Aureolus, Hypnotic Gaze, Stroke of Luck all fit), cancel attack/damage/horror/encounter (Hypnotic Gaze, I've had worse, Ward of Protection, Dr. Maleson), draw/search/shuffle, gain-resource, doom add/remove (Blood Pact, Moonlight Ritual, Alyssa), move investigator/enemy + Lure's enemy-control, attach asset/enemy/location, slot/charisma/relic-hunter additions, succeed/fail-by, BuffStatsReplace (correctly handles every 'use willpower instead of intellect/combat/agility' case e.g. Rite of Seeking, Shrivelling, Song of the Dead, Bind Monster), enemy-value reads/reductions (Expose Weakness, If it bleeds), tank/soak (Brother Xavier, Peter Sylvestre), recursion-to-hand (Try and Try Again, Opportunist), and the rich timing/duration vocabularies.

GENUINE GAPS proposed above: (1) base-stat override to a fixed number (distinct from BuffStatsReplace's stat-swap and from +N boosts); (2) exile (a NEW dwl keyword with deckbuilding/XP implications, currently emitted by regex but with no tag); (3) put-a-card-into-play from deck/discard/hand; (4) redirect an enemy attack's damage onto another enemy; (5) transfer/give assets+resources between investigators; (6) grant extra/immediate actions; (7) max-hand-size increase; (8) look-at/reorder top of deck (scry / encounter-deck smoothing).

AMBIGUITIES / judgment calls for the synthesizer: (a) ActionAdditional already exists with an optional value and canOnlyBeUsedTo field — it MAY be intended to also cover 'gain N actions', but its doc comment ('Assume 1 action if not specified') reads as describing an ability's action COST/restriction, not an action GRANT; I proposed a distinct grant variant but flag this as possibly an argument-extension instead. (b) Exile could be a variant under discard/from-play OR its own category; I lean toward its own keyword tag because it is a deckbuilding concept, not a discard destination. (c) 'rfg_self' (remove-from-game, e.g. Lucky Dice 'remove Lucky Dice from the game', Gold Pocket Watch 'remove from the game') and 'exile' are related but distinct (exile = returns to collection / repurchasable; rfg = gone for the scenario); the digest covers neither — I folded exile into a proposal but left generic remove-from-game unproposed pending whether it's wanted. (d) Quick Thinking's extra action is conditional on succeed-by-2; I still treat the action-grant as the searchable effect. (e) The Gold Pocket Watch's skip/repeat-phase effect (02305) is a genuinely unique, non-recurring effect I did NOT propose a tag for (too rare to be a useful search axis), but flagging it here for completeness.

args.name: from
args.type: SkillType (the stat whose value is ADDED on top)

args.name: action
args.type: TestingBasicAction (optional: fight/investigate/evade the addition applies to)

proposedTags.rationale: Distinct from the existing BuffStatsReplace (which models 'uses [X] INSTEAD OF [Y]'). These cards keep the base stat and ADD a second stat's value on top, a different and very searchable deckbuilding effect. Sweeping Kick (08023): 'Add your [agility] to your skill value for this attack.' Fang of Tyr'thrha (08029): 'Add your [agility] to your [combat] for this attack.' Cyclopean Hammer (08093): 'Add your [willpower] to your skill value for this attack.' Butterfly Swords (08025/08030): 'fight again, adding your [agility] to your skill value.' The codebase already flags this gap explicitly: tags/src/tagged-cards/rcore.ts line 1783 has the comment '// stat_add_agility_for_investigate - Need tag type', and the old regex tag stat_add_agility_for_attack / stat_add_willpower_for_attack appears on these very cards.

args.name: value
args.type: number (count of cards looked at, e.g. 3, 5, 6; -1 for variable)

proposedTags.rationale: Looking at the top N cards of a deck and optionally reordering them (scry / top-deck manipulation) has no tag; it is a recurring divination/seeker/fortune archetype players search for. Parallel Fates (08066): 'Look at the top 6 cards of an investigator's deck or the encounter deck. You may either return them to the top of that deck in any order, or shuffle them.' Jeremiah Kirby (08032): 'Reveal the top 5 cards of your deck. Draw each card with a cost that matches...' Astronomical Atlas (08067): 'Look at the top card of your deck. If it is not a weakness, attach it facedown...' The codebase already flags this gap: tags/src/tagged-cards/rcore.ts lines 1031-1034 carry comments '// look_at_encounter - Need tag type', '// order_encounter - Need tag type'.

args.name: value
args.type: number (count of cards looked at; -1 for variable)

proposedTags.rationale: Same scry archetype but targeting the ENCOUNTER deck — searched separately because it is encounter-control tech rather than self card-selection. Parallel Fates (08066): 'Look at the top 6 cards of an investigator's deck or the encounter deck...' Counterespionage (08049): cancels a treachery then redraws/manipulates the encounter (and an upgrade redirects to 'your deck'). Foresight (08064): 'Play when an investigator would draw a card from their deck or from the encounter deck. Name a card. If the drawn card is the named card...' Same '// look_at_encounter / order_encounter - Need tag type' comments at rcore.ts 1031-1034 confirm the gap.

args.name: zone
args.type: 'discard' | 'top-deck' | 'hand-other-investigator' | 'set-aside' (where the card is played from / who may play it)

proposedTags.rationale: Letting a card be played from a zone other than the owner's hand, or by an investigator other than the owner, is a recurring rogue/economy archetype with no tag (the existing play-area folder only moves cards FROM play TO hand/deck). Untimely Transaction (08051): 'Another investigator at your location may play that asset as if it were in their hand.' Black Market (08055): 'While set aside... any investigator may play any of those cards as if they were in their hand.' True Magick (08070): 'You may resolve abilities on [[Spell]] assets in your hand by revealing them from your hand.' Shrewd Dealings (08017): 'Play it under the control of any investigator at your location.' Distinct from Recursion (which returns cards to hand first).

Committing cards to skill tests from a zone OTHER than hand is a distinctive Norman Withers / fortune-teller archetype with no tag (committing from hand is the default and intentionally untagged). Livre d'Eibon (08002... 08016 range, code 08016 'Livre d'Eibon'): 'Commit the top card of your deck to an eligible skill test.' Written in the Stars (08034): 'while that card is in your discard pile, commit it to each eligible skill test you perform.' Astronomical Atlas (08067): 'Commit a card attached to Astronomical Atlas to an eligible skill test.' Searchable because it enables deck-top/discard-fueled commit engines.

args.name: perClass
args.type: number (resources gained per different class among cards you control)

proposedTags.rationale: Existing GainResourceYou takes a fixed numeric value, but a cluster of eote cards scale by 'different class among cards you control' — a dynamic value the current fixed-value field cannot express. Cheat the System (08050): 'Gain 1 resource for each different class among cards you control.' This pairs with the multiclass archetype below. Proposed as a sibling to GainResourceYou rather than a value because the COUNT is the searchable hook (big-money / multiclass payoff).

A signature eote mechanic with no tag: effects that scale with the number of different classes among cards you control (rewarding multiclass/five-color decks). Gang Up (08022): 'For each different class among cards you control, you get +1 [combat] and deal +1 damage.' Strength in Numbers (08077): 'gains a [wild] icon for each different class among cards you control.' Close the Circle (08062): 'Uses (1 charge for each class among cards you control).' Call for Backup (08129): one effect per class controlled. Join the Caravan (08036): 'Reduce the cost of this card by 1 for each different class among cards you control.' This is the unifying searchable hook for the whole multiclass sub-theme.

'Big money' rogue payoffs that grant bonuses while you hold a threshold of resources have no tag and are a distinct searchable archetype. The Black Fan (08057): 'While you have... 10+ resources, +1 health and +1 sanity; ...15+ resources, one additional action; ...20+ resources, +1 to each skill.' Money Talks (08054): base skill value 'equal to half the number of resources in your resource pool.' Pairs with GainResourceDynamicClassCount and the large GainResource values (Unscrupulous Loan 08113 gains 10) as a big-money compound.

args.name: restrictedTo
args.type: trait string (e.g. 'Creature' — the trait the extra slot is restricted to)

proposedTags.rationale: SlotAdditionalAlly exists, but eote introduces ally slots RESTRICTED to a trait, which is a different deckbuilding constraint worth filtering. Rod of Animalism (08128): 'You have 2 additional ally slots, which can only be used to hold [[Creature]] assets.' If preferred, this could instead be a 'restrictedTo' argument added to the existing SlotAdditionalAlly tag rather than a new variant — flagging for the synthesizer's choice.

proposedCompoundTags.conceptDescription: Cards that reward controlling many different classes (the five-color / 'rainbow' deckbuilding payoff), scaling combat, damage, resources, wild icons, cost reduction, or charges by the number of different classes among cards you control.
proposedCompoundTags.rationale: eote is built around a multiclass theme and several cards independently key off 'different class among cards you control': Gang Up (08022), Strength in Numbers (08077), Close the Circle (08062), Cheat the System (08050), Call for Backup (08129), Join the Caravan (08036). Players search this as one archetype when building rainbow decks; a compound tag groups the distinct base effects (stat boost, wild icons, resources, cost reduction, charges) under it.

proposedCompoundTags.conceptDescription: Resource-acceleration and resource-threshold payoff package: large lump-sum resource gains plus effects that reward or scale off a high resource pool.
proposedCompoundTags.rationale: A recurring rogue archetype players deckbuild around. eote examples: The Black Fan (08057, threshold bonuses at 10/15/20 resources), Money Talks (08054, skill value from resource pool), Unscrupulous Loan (08113, 'Gain 10 resources'), 21 or Bust (08048, gain 4-9 resources), Cheat the System (08050). Groups the threshold tag with the high-value GainResource tags so 'big money' decks are findable as one cluster.

proposedCompoundTags.conceptDescription: Top-deck / draw-manipulation tech: looking at, reordering, or pre-selecting the top cards of player or encounter decks, including swapping deck-top with hand and naming-then-cancelling an incoming draw.
proposedCompoundTags.rationale: A distinct 'control what you draw' archetype mirroring the existing clue-tech / chaos-control compounds. eote examples: Parallel Fates (08066), Jeremiah Kirby (08032), Astronomical Atlas (08067), Foresight (08064), Counterespionage (08049), Livre d'Eibon (08016, swap deck-top with hand). Groups player-deck scry, encounter-deck scry, and deck-top commit so divination/foresight decks are searchable together.

archetypes.name: Multiclass / rainbow payoff
archetypes.description: Cards that scale with the number of different classes among cards you control, rewarding five-color decks. The defining new theme of eote. Effects span stat boosts, wild icons, resources, cost reduction, and charges.

archetypes.name: Big-money rogue / resource threshold
archetypes.description: Resource acceleration plus payoffs that scale off or trigger at a high resource pool (10/15/20+), including lump-sum gains and resource-as-skill-value.

archetypes.name: Stat-add (additive, not replacement)
archetypes.description: Add a second skill's value on top of the base skill for an attack/investigate/evade, as opposed to fully replacing it. Heavy in eote weapons and martial-arts cards.

archetypes.name: Deck-top control / divination
archetypes.description: Look at, reorder, name, or pre-select top cards of player or encounter decks; commit from deck-top or discard. A seeker/mystic foresight archetype.

archetypes.name: Play-from-other-zone economy
archetypes.description: Play cards from discard, set-aside, or another investigator's hand, or under another's control. A rogue/multiplayer flexibility archetype.

archetypes.name: Leyline / Archive of Conduits engine
archetypes.description: Place resources as leylines on locations, then move/spend them for movement, investigation, evasion, damage, or draw. Self-contained eote signature engine (researched customizable).

coverageNotes:
EXISTING TAXONOMY ALREADY COVERS WELL (do not re-propose): stat boosts in/out of test (boost-in-test, boost-passive, stats-mod-pump for charge/resource scaling like Sledgehammer/Brand of Cthugha); bold actions (fight/evade/investigate/move); damage-plus with value (Sledgehammer +5, Fang +3); uses (charge/ammo/secret/supply/durability/resource AND the leyline 'uses-type-leylines' the old tags use) with uses-starting value and uses-replenish (Prophetic/True Magick/Sleuth/Bruiser/Crafty/Antiquary); deck-restriction & limit-1-per-deck/per-investigator & purchase-at-deck-creation; gain-resource with fixed value; draw-player with value; heal with value+target (incl. investigator/ally support); succeed-by / fail-by (Test result, succeed-by-0/2/3); chaos-reveal-token-* and chaos-seal-* and chaos-effect (21 or Bust 08048, Snipe 08087, Nkosi 08091, Heavy Furs 08126 reveal-another-instead, 'Hit me!' 08112 reveal-more); cost-reaction/fast/free with exhaust/spend/discard/damage-self; ADDITIONAL ACTION is covered by TagTypeActionAdditional.ActionAdditional (Red Clock 08053/08058, Blur 08109/08111, Black Fan 08057) — do NOT propose a new tag for it; trait-support (the 'spend on X/Y/Z trait cards' cards 08120-08124 map to trait-support-*); cost-discount (Shrewd Dealings, Geared Up, Rod of Animalism); slot-additional (arcane: Dragon Pole 08060; ally: Rod of Animalism); testless clue/damage/evade; cancel-revelation/horror (Counterespionage, Protective Gear 08095, Talisman 08116); engage-with-you / elite-unusable (elite_unusable widely); BuffStatsReplace covers 'use [X] INSTEAD OF [Y]' for attacks/evades/investigations (Brand of Cthugha 08090/08092, Divination 08101/08103, Blur, Enchanted Bow 08118, Close the Circle 08062) — these are NOT gaps.

KEY DISTINCTION I RELIED ON: BuffStatsReplace = replacement ('instead of'); the proposed StatsModAddSkillForAction = additive ('ADD your X to your skill value', keeping the base stat). The codebase confirms the additive case is unhandled via the literal comment at tags/src/tagged-cards/rcore.ts:1783 ('// stat_add_agility_for_investigate - Need tag type') and the deck-scry gap via comments at rcore.ts:1031-1034 ('// look_at_encounter / order_encounter - Need tag type').

AMBIGUITIES / FLAGS: (1) SlotAdditionalCreatureAlly (08128) might be better modeled as a 'restrictedTo' argument on the existing SlotAdditionalAlly rather than a new variant — left as a choice for synthesis. (2) GainResourceDynamicClassCount overlaps with MulticlassClassCount; I proposed both because the resource gain is also a 'big-money' hook, but a synthesizer may prefer to fold it into MulticlassClassCount with reward='resource'. (3) The leyline/Archive of Conduits engine (08033, 08041-08044) is a self-contained customizable engine; its sub-effects (place resource as leyline on locations, move leyline, spend to grant move/investigate/evade/draw/damage) are mostly expressible piecemeal via existing move/draw/heal/testless tags, so I did NOT propose a dedicated leyline tag — flagging in case a later global pass wants a 'resource-on-location/leyline' tag if the pattern recurs. (4) 'Written in the Stars' (08034) and Astronomical Atlas (08067) also do deck-top filtering that overlaps both the scry and commit-from-non-hand proposals; I split them by mechanic (scry = look/reorder; commit-non-hand = actually committing) to keep tags atomic. (5) Defensive Stance (08024), Survey the Area (08037), Occult Theory (08065), Dauntless Spirit (08078) 'gains [X] icons equal to your [Y]' while in hand/committed: this is the in-hand icon-swap pattern — arguably BuffStatsReplace-adjacent but about COMMITTED ICONS not skill value; currently untagged (these have empty tag arrays). I did not propose a new tag because it is a niche static-icon effect, but flag it as a possible future 'commit-icon-from-stat' gap.

proposedTags.rationale: The Codex of Ages (90082) reads 'Seal ([elder_sign] or up to 3 [bless])'. The chaos/seal.ts enum has ChaosSealTokenElderSign, ElderThing, Cultist, Skull, Tablet, Any, AutoFail, Token0 — but NO Bless variant. Bless-seal is its own searchable mechanic (bless/curse decks want cards that lock bless tokens onto a card), and the reveal side already distinguishes ChaosRevealTokenBless, so the seal side should mirror it. Conservative single-sibling addition to an existing enum.

The Codex of Ages (90082): '[reaction] When an investigator ... would reveal a chaos token from the chaos bag: That investigator resolves a token sealed here instead, then releases that token.' This substitutes a pre-selected SEALED token for the random bag draw — distinct from ChaosRevealAnotherInstead (reveal another random token) and from ChaosRevealManual (manually pick). It is the core of the 'controlled token via sealing' archetype (Codex of Ages, Grotesque Statue-adjacent sealed-token swaps). Belongs as a sibling in chaos/reveal.ts.

Ruth Westmacott (98020): 'Reduce the difficulty of this skill test by 2.' This lowers the test's target number, which is mechanically different from StatsModBoostInTest* (raising your own skill value) and from LocationShroud* (shroud is the difficulty only of investigate tests). No existing tag captures generic skill-test-difficulty reduction. Recurring archetype (Counterspell-style, 'reduce the difficulty' enemy/treachery tech). New folder test-difficulty (sibling to skill-value/test).

Mystifying Song (99002): 'Until the end of the phase, the agenda cannot advance by reaching its doom threshold.' DoomAdd/DoomCheck/DoomRemove cover changing doom counts, but none cover PREVENTING the agenda from advancing when its threshold is met. This is a distinct, highly searchable 'stall the agenda / buy a turn' archetype (Mystifying Song, Time Warp-adjacent). New file under the existing doom folder.

Mysteries Remain (98005): 'Either place 1 clue (from the token bank) on your location, or discover 1 clue at your location.' PLACING a clue on a location (adding a clue token from the bank) is distinct from DISCOVERING a clue (ClueDiscover*) — placing creates a clue to be collected later / can fuel act progress or other 'when a clue is placed' tech. ClueAdditional is about discovering extra clues during an investigation, not placing. Recurring archetype (clue-placement / 'seed a clue' cards). New file in the clue folder.

Split the Angle (98008): '[free] Exhaust Split the Angle and discard the top card of your deck: Discard the top card of the encounter deck.' Proactively discarding/thinning the ENCOUNTER deck is a control archetype (encounter-deck scry/thin, e.g. Scroll of Secrets, 'Eat the Bullet'-adjacent). DeckDiscardDeck/DeckDiscardSelf target the player deck/self; DeckSearchEncounter is look-at-top, not discard. Add a sibling enum value in deck/discard.ts for encounter-deck discard.

proposedCompoundTags.conceptDescription: Cards that manipulate the chaos bag draw / token outcomes: revealing more or another token, ignoring/cancelling token effects, sealing tokens away, resolving a sealed token instead of the random draw, and treating tokens as something else. Players search this whole cluster together when building token-control / bless-curse / 'mitigate the bag' decks.
proposedCompoundTags.rationale: The digest has many granular chaos/seal, chaos/reveal, chaos/effect tags and a CancelChaos tag, but NO compound grouping them, even though the prompt explicitly names 'chaos-token control (reveal-more / ignore / cancel / seal / check-what-is-revealed)' as a target archetype. The Codex of Ages (90082) is a perfect anchor: it seals tokens (incl. bless) and resolves a sealed token instead of the bag draw — pure token control. Reality Acid (89005) reveals more tokens on auto_fail. This pack is the first to motivate formalizing the cluster.

archetypes.name: Sealed-Token Bag Control (bless / elder sign substitution)
archetypes.description: Seal specific chaos tokens (elder sign, bless) onto a card and later substitute one of those sealed tokens for the random bag draw, guaranteeing the outcome. Combines token sealing (incl. the missing Bless-seal) with 'resolve a sealed token instead of revealing'. A recurring bless/holy and elder-sign-fishing archetype.

archetypes.name: Agenda Stall / Anti-Advance
archetypes.description: Effects that prevent the agenda from advancing when it reaches its doom threshold (or otherwise buy the team time) without removing doom. Distinct from doom-removal; the searchable thing is 'I cannot afford to lose the round yet'.

archetypes.name: Encounter-Deck Manipulation / Scry-Thin
archetypes.description: Look at, reveal, and proactively discard cards off the top of the encounter deck to control what the team draws in the mythos phase. A control/support archetype distinct from player-deck draw/discard.

archetypes.name: Skill-Test Difficulty Reduction
archetypes.description: Lower the difficulty (target number) of a skill test directly, rather than boosting your own skill value. Often enemy/treachery-facing tech that makes hard tests trivially passable for the whole team.

archetypes.name: Devour Engine (Subject 5U-21 campaign-specific)
archetypes.description: Place player/encounter cards 'beneath' a permanent to grow a scaling all-skills bonus, then optionally regurgitate them for healing. Campaign-locked (Subject 5U-21) and not a general deckbuilding mechanic, but the underlying effects (passive +all-skills boost, heal-per-card) are already covered by StatsModBoostPassiveAny and Heal* tags.

coverageNotes:
This 'etc' pack is 13 signature/replacement/parallel-investigator cards (deck_restriction or Replacement), so many effects are already well covered and several are campaign-locked one-offs.

ALREADY COVERED WELL (do NOT re-tag): passive '+1 to each of your skills' boosts (Ravenous 89002, Foolishness 98011, Codex of Ages 90082) map to StatsModBoostPassiveAny; Jenny's Twin .45s (90085) fight +2 combat / +1 damage / exhaust-cost-reaction map to ActionBoldFight + StatsModBoostInTestCombat + DamagePlus(1) + CostReactionExhaustSelf; Regurgitation (89003) heal 1 damage/horror = HealDamageYou/HealHorrorYou and is fast-during-turn (TimingDuringYourTurn); Reality Acid (89005) auto_fail 'Reveal 3 more chaos tokens' = ChaosRevealMore and the per-token table is ChaosRevealToken* (already largely tagged); Nautical Prowess (98014) 'draw 1 card' = DeckDrawYou; Molly Maxwell (98017) 'reveal cards from the top of your deck until an asset with the named trait... shuffle the rest back' = DeckSearchYou (range all); Mysteries Remain's (98005) 'discover 1 clue at your location' = ClueDiscoverYourLocation; deck restrictions = DeckRestriction; exhaust-as-cost = CostFastExhaustSelf.

GAPS (proposed above): bless-seal (ChaosSealTokenBless), resolve-sealed-token-instead-of-bag-draw, skill-test difficulty reduction, prevent-agenda-advance, place-a-clue (vs discover), encounter-deck discard/thin, plus a chaos-token-control compound that the digest conspicuously lacks.

ARGUMENT-EXTENSION CANDIDATE (flagged, not a new tag): Jenny's Twin .45s (90085) 'Gain resources equal to that enemy's printed health' — GainResourceYou requires a fixed numeric value; this is a DYNAMIC, on-defeat resource gain. Consider allowing a dynamic/variable marker (e.g. value -1 or a 'dynamic'/'onDefeat' qualifier) on TagGainResource* rather than a new tag. I did not formally propose it because the broad searchable aspect ('gain resources') is already the tag; only the dynamic source is new.

AMBIGUITIES I could not fully resolve: (1) 'devour' (Ravenous/Regurgitation/Reality Acid, Subject 5U-21 only) is a campaign keyword that removes player/encounter cards into a hidden zone — arguably a removal/recursion-adjacent effect, but it is so campaign-locked and idiosyncratic that I treated it as non-searchable for deckbuilding rather than minting tags. (2) Green Man Medallion (98002) 'reduce the experience cost of the next card you purchase by 1' is a between-scenario XP-economy effect with no analog anywhere in the taxonomy; it is a true singleton here, so I did NOT propose a tag, but flag it for the global synthesis in case other meta/campaign cards share it. (3) Split the Angle's '[action]: Reveal the top card of the encounter deck' is a look-at-top effect that could alternatively be modeled as DeckSearchEncounter(range top:1); I leaned toward the separate encounter-discard tag only for the discard half.

proposedTags.rationale: The existing chaos/reveal.ts only tags REACTING to a revealed token (ChaosRevealTokenBless). There is no tag for ADDING bless tokens TO the bag, which is the entire engine of the Blessed archetype and is rampant in this pack. The old regex collapses both into 'chaos_reveal_token_bless', losing the distinction. Keep Faith: 'Add 4 [bless] tokens to the chaos bag.' Guided by Faith: 'add 2 [bless] tokens to the chaos bag.' Blessed Blade: 'add 2 [bless] tokens to the chaos bag.' Absolution: 'add 1 [bless] token to the chaos bag.' value = number added (use -1 for X/variable).

Mirror of ChaosBagAddBless for the Cursed archetype, also missing from the taxonomy. Many Cursed cards pay a cost of seeding the bag with curses. Scrimshaw Charm: 'Add 1-3 [curse] tokens to the chaos bag... Gain 1 resource.' Prismatic Spectacles: 'Add 1 [curse] token to the chaos bag.' Wicked Athame: 'Add 1-3 [curse] tokens to the chaos bag.' Esoteric Method: 'add 1 [curse] token to the chaos bag for each point...succeeded or failed by.' Gabriel Carillo: 'add 1 [curse] token to the chaos bag: Draw 1 card.'

Removing tokens FROM the bag is a distinct searchable effect (bag-thinning / balance control) with no existing tag. The Key of Solomon: 'remove 1 [bless] token from the chaos bag and exhaust...: Heal up to 2 damage...'. Purified: 'add 1 [bless] token or remove 1 [curse] token from the chaos bag.' Twilight Diadem treats a token as elder sign 'returning it to the chaos bag' (returns, not removes — exclude). Distinct from sealing (which holds on a card).

Mirror of ChaosBagRemoveBless; curse-pulling is a key counter-tech for cursed decks. The Key of Solomon: 'remove 1 [curse] token from the chaos bag and exhaust...: Gain 2 resources.' Purified: '...or remove 1 [curse] token from the chaos bag.'

chaos/effect.ts has ChaosEffectIgnoreModifier (ignore the modifier entirely) but a 'treat the modifier as 0' is a specific, repeated wording players search for as curse-mitigation that may differ subtly from full ignore. Accursed: 'treat the modifier of each [curse] token revealed as 0.' Dawn Star: 'Ignore the modifiers of each [curse] token revealed.' If judged equivalent to ChaosEffectIgnoreModifier, fold these into that tag instead — flagged as possible duplicate.

chaos/reveal.ts has ChaosRevealAnotherInstead (reveal a different token instead) and ChaosEffectResolveChoose. But 'search the bag for a specific token and resolve IT instead of what would be revealed' is a distinct control effect. Book of Living Myths: 'When a chaos token would be revealed... Search the chaos bag for a [bless] or [curse] token... and resolve it instead.' Evanescent Ascension resolves an elder sign effect in addition. If ChaosRevealAnotherInstead already covers 'pick a specific token from bag and resolve it', fold in — flagged.

A repeated 'cancel a revealed token, return it to the bag, and reveal a new one' effect (redraw/reroll a token) that ChaosRevealMore (reveal extra) and ChaosRevealAnotherInstead (substitute before reveal) do not capture — this is a post-reveal re-draw. Strong-Armed: 'After revealing chaos token(s)... you may take 1 damage to cancel that chaos token, return it to the chaos bag, and reveal a new one.' Token of Faith re-attempts the test. Distinct token-fishing tech.

enemy/debuff.ts has EnemyDoesNotReady and EnemyCannotMoveIntoLocation but no 'attached enemy cannot attack' debuff, a recurring lock-down effect (Rot attachments / handler cards). Abyssal Rot: 'Attached enemy cannot attack.' Pairs with the enemy-disable archetype. (Virescent Rot 'cannot move' and Putrescent Rot stat reductions are arguably also gaps but lower priority.)

Companion to EnemyCannotAttack; 'attached enemy cannot move' is distinct enemy field-control not covered by EnemyCannotMoveIntoLocation (which is about a location, not the enemy itself). Virescent Rot: 'Attached enemy cannot move.' Transmogrify grants attached enemy 'Cannot move.'

Forcing an enemy to disengage from investigators is a distinct evasion/control effect with no existing tag (engage/*.ts covers engaging, not forced disengage of an enemy). Blackmail File: 'that enemy disengages from each investigator and gains aloof.' Stir the Pot: 'you may disengage from each enemy and move' (investigator-side disengage — borderline). Searchable enemy-control tech.

uses/starting.ts enumerates Ammo/Charge/Supply/Secret/Evidence but NOT offerings, a brand-new use-type that is the core resource of the entire Mask sub-archetype in this pack. The old regex even invented 'uses_type_offerings'/'uses_starting_2' with no backing enum. Wolf Mask: 'Uses (2 offerings).' Speak to the Dead: 'Uses (6 offerings).' Bianca: 'Uses (10 resources)' (resources is also unlisted). Needs an offering (and likely resource) starting-use variant.

'Uses (N resources)' as a printed use-pool is unrepresented in uses/starting.ts. Bianca "Die Katz": 'Uses (10 resources).' Distinct from gaining resources to your pool. Lower priority but a genuine enum gap surfaced by the old regex tag 'uses_type_resource'.

The old regex emits a 'uses_replenish' hint but there is NO replenish tag anywhere in the taxonomy. Conditional/triggered replenishment of a use-pool is a strong recurring mechanic (esp. Masks and Ofuda). Ofuda: 'Replenish this charge the first time a [bless] token is revealed at your location each round.' Wolf Mask: 'Replenish 1 of these offerings after you engage an enemy.' Wicked Athame: 'replenish 1 charge or offering on an asset you control.' Call the Beyond: 'Replenish all of that asset's charges or secrets.' This is the missing 'use-economy refuel' archetype.

attach/main.ts has AttachEnemy (generic) which already covers these, so this may be redundant — flagged for the synthesizer. Mentioned only because Beguile/Transmogrify/Rod-of-Carnamagos all attach control cards to enemies as a parley/evasion package; if AttachEnemy is the searchable unit, prefer it and DROP this. Listing to surface the cluster, not to duplicate.

A repeated 'swap this card with its bonded partner, moving tokens/charges' mechanic (transforming weapon/diadem) with no existing tag. Eyes of Valusia: 'Search your bonded cards for Blade of Yoth and swap it... moving all charges.' Blade of Yoth swaps back. Broken Diadem swaps with Twilight Diadem 'moving all offerings.' Flux Stabilizer flips sides. This 'transform/flip into bonded upgrade' is a distinct deckbuilding archetype searchable as a unit.

gain/resource.ts covers gaining resources to a pool, but MOVING resources between investigators' pools (resource sharing/loan) is distinct and unrepresented. "I'll Pay You Back!": 'Move all resources from that investigator's resource pool to your resource pool... At the end of the round, move all resources... back.' Bank Job and Grift distribute resources to investigators at your location (multiplayer big-money support). Pairs into a resource-economy compound.

action/additional.ts ActionAdditional covers gaining an additional action for THIS activation/effect, but a card that grants extra actions on a FUTURE turn is a distinct tempo effect. Bide Your Time: 'During your next turn, you may take two additional actions.' If ActionAdditional is deemed broad enough to cover deferred actions, fold in — flagged. value = number of extra actions.

recursion/main.ts (RecursionAsset/Event/Skill) and discard-pile/main.ts (to hand/deck) exist, but 'resolve/play a card DIRECTLY from your discard pile' (without first returning it to hand) is a distinct, searchable recursion style. Pushed to the Limit: 'Choose a Weapon or Tool asset in your discard pile. Resolve an [action] ability on that asset.' Eldritch Tongue: 'play events with "parley" from your discard pile as if they were in your hand.' Persistence: 'commit Persistence to a skill test from your discard pile.' Speak to the Dead returns events from discard. Strong cross-pack archetype (flashback/graveyard value).

A recurring 'resolve an [action]/[fast] ability on another asset without paying its cost' tempo/combo enabler with no existing tag. Hand-Eye Coordination: 'Resolve an [action] ability on a [[Tool]] or [[Weapon]] asset you control without paying its [action] cost.' Dirty Deeds: 'resolve an [action] or [fast] ability on that asset, ignoring all costs.' Ad Hoc, "Throw the Book at Them!", Task Force, Flurry of Blows, Call the Beyond all reuse this. Major action-compression archetype.

proposedCompoundTags.conceptDescription: Cards that manipulate the composition of the chaos bag by adding or removing bless/curse tokens — the engine of the Blessed and Cursed archetypes. Players building these decks search this cluster as a unit (seed the bag, thin the bag, balance bless vs curse).
proposedCompoundTags.rationale: These four proposed base tags are mechanically distinct (add vs remove, bless vs curse) but are deckbuilt together. Keep Faith adds 4 bless; Scrimshaw Charm adds curses for resources; The Key of Solomon removes bless OR curse depending on bag balance; Purified 'add 1 [bless] or remove 1 [curse]'. A single archetype query should surface the whole Blessed/Cursed token-economy package.

proposedCompoundTags.conceptDescription: Broad chaos-token control: reveal-more, ignore/cancel modifiers, treat-as, re-draw a revealed token, resolve-a-chosen-token-instead. The grouping players use for 'mitigate the bad token' tech.
proposedCompoundTags.rationale: Olive McBride (reveal 4 choose 2, ignore rest), Strong-Armed (return token, redraw), Accursed/Dawn Star (treat curse modifier as 0/ignore), Book of Living Myths (resolve a chosen token instead), Twilight Diadem (treat as elder sign). All are 'control what the bag does to my test' and are searched together even though they live in different chaos/* files.

proposedCompoundTags.conceptDescription: Cards whose value is refilling limited-use pools (charges, offerings, ammo, secrets) — replenish triggers and effects that recharge another asset. The 'never run out of ammo/charges' engine.
proposedCompoundTags.rationale: Ofuda, the Masks, Wicked Athame ('replenish 1 charge or offering on an asset you control'), and Call the Beyond ('Replenish all of that asset's charges or secrets') form a refuel package distinct from simply having starting uses. The old regex's invented 'uses_replenish' hint shows this concept is wanted but has no backing tag.

proposedCompoundTags.conceptDescription: Cards that let you resolve another card's [action]/[fast] ability without paying its action cost, take an immediate extra attack/action, or bank actions for a future turn — tempo/combo enablers searched together by efficiency-focused deckbuilders.
proposedCompoundTags.rationale: Hand-Eye Coordination, Dirty Deeds, "Throw the Book at Them!", Flurry of Blows ('take an immediate fight action... without paying its [action] cost'), and Bide Your Time all compress or generate actions. Existing ActionAdditional is one member; the activate-without-cost effect is the recurring missing piece that ties the cluster together.

proposedCompoundTags.conceptDescription: Big-money / resource-economy cards: generate large resource bursts, move resources between investigators, or care about having zero resources. The grouping for resource-fueled (Dark Horse / smuggler) builds.
proposedCompoundTags.rationale: Bank Job (8 resources distributed), Grift (up to 6 from a parley), "I'll Pay You Back!" (move resources between pools), Dark Horse (rewards zero resources) cluster into a resource-tempo archetype. GainResource already exists; ResourceMoveInvestigator is the missing connective tag. Surfaces the cross-pack 'big money' theme the rubric explicitly calls out.

archetypes.name: Blessed token economy
archetypes.description: Seed the chaos bag with [bless] tokens, reward revealing them (heal, extra clues, draw), and convert/clean curses. Built around adding bless to the bag rather than just reacting to it — the missing ChaosBagAddBless/RemoveCurse tags are central.

archetypes.name: Cursed token economy
archetypes.description: Intentionally pay the cost of adding [curse] tokens to the chaos bag for powerful payoffs (resources, damage, clues, draw), then mitigate the downside (treat curse modifier as 0, ignore, pull curses). Centers on ChaosBagAddCurse and curse-mitigation control.

archetypes.name: Mask / offering toolkit
archetypes.description: The [[Mask]] sub-theme: assets with 'Uses (N offerings)' replenished by varied triggers, spent for flexible +2 skill boosts. Needs UsesStartingOffering and conditional replenish tags; otherwise well-served by existing boost tags.

archetypes.name: Parley control package
archetypes.description: Parley actions that test against an enemy's own stat (X = health/fight/evade) to evade, disengage, exhaust-lock, gain resources, or move it. Existing bold_parley + initiate_test_*_x cover the test framing; gaps are forced enemy disengage and enemy stat-lock.

archetypes.name: Enemy attachment / Rot lock-down
archetypes.description: Attach a control card to a non-Elite enemy that disables it (cannot attack / cannot move / stat reduction / takes damage each round). Driven by Rod of Carnamagos + Rot events and Transmogrify/Beguile. Needs EnemyCannotAttack/EnemyCannotMove.

archetypes.name: Discard-pile recursion / flashback
archetypes.description: Play or resolve cards directly from the discard pile (events, weapon/tool actions, skill commits) without first returning them to hand. A distinct graveyard-value style needing RecursionFromDiscardPlay.

archetypes.name: Action-compression / combo tempo
archetypes.description: Resolve another asset's ability without paying its action cost, chain immediate attacks, or bank future actions. Wilson/Tool-Weapon and Illicit combo shells lean on this.

archetypes.name: Transforming bonded gear
archetypes.description: Cards that swap with a bonded partner (or flip sides), carrying charges/offerings across, to upgrade a weapon/diadem mid-scenario. Needs BondedSwap.

archetypes.name: Resource big-money support
archetypes.description: Generate large resource bursts and shuttle resources between investigators; payoff cards reward an empty or full resource pool. Multiplayer-leaning economy support.

coverageNotes:
Pack analyzed: 123 cards (codes 10002-10134), the player cards of The Feast of Hemlock Vale (fhv).

ALREADY WELL COVERED (do not re-propose): bold action declarations (bold_fight/evade/investigate/parley) via TagTypeActionBold; stat boosts +N per skill via stats-mod/boost-in-test + boost-passive (Katana, Masks, Microscope all fit, incl. boost-any); using one stat instead of another (Aetheric Current 'intellect instead of combat') via buff/stats-replace; 'add your X to your skill value' (Ethereal Form, Spectral Razor, Read the Signs) via the stat_add_*_for_* tags the regex already references; damage_plus_N via damage/main; testless clue/damage/evade via testless/*; clue discovery and additional clues via clue/discover + clue/additional (Snitch, Microscope, Chemistry Set); shroud reduction (Matchbox) via location/shroud; initiating a test of skill X at difficulty Y/X via test/initiate (the regex 'initiate_test_*_x/_0/_1' maps here); succeed/fail-by margins via skill-value/* and test/result (Chemistry Set 'succeed by exactly 2', Steady-Handed); uses starting counts for ammo/charge/supply/secret/evidence via uses/starting; supply/ammo sharing (Cleaning Kit) via uses/support; costs (exhaust/discard/spend resource/charge/secret, damage-self) via cost/*; healing via heal/main; card draw via deck/draw; deck search via deck/search (Bewitching, Dirty Deeds, bonded searches); discard-pile-to-hand via discard-pile/main; auto-evade / auto-success via auto/main (Lightfooted, Confound's 'automatically evade'); reveal-token reactions via chaos/reveal; seal via chaos/seal; cancel-treachery (Ravenous Myconid) via cancel/CancelRevelation+CancelEncounterEffect; doom add (Esoteric adds curse not doom; but Vamp removes doom — doom/DoomRemove covers it); deck restriction / limit-per-deck / max-committed flagged by deck/misc and the regex limit tags; traits via trait/support; elite-unusable (non-Elite only) via enemy/elite.

PRIMARY GAP (highest confidence, cross-pack): the chaos taxonomy only models REACTING TO revealed tokens; it cannot express ADDING tokens to the bag or REMOVING tokens from the bag. This is the core of Blessed/Cursed deckbuilding and the old regex wrongly collapses 'add bless' into 'chaos_reveal_token_bless'. Proposed ChaosBagAdd/Remove Bless/Curse (new chaos/bag.ts) + the bless-curse-bag-control compound are the most important additions. Note: I treated 'return a token to the bag' (Twilight Diadem, Blessed Blade's 'return each bless revealed') as NOT a removal — it is a return, so excluded from Remove tags; flag for synthesis whether a separate 'return-to-bag' concept is wanted.

SECONDARY GAPS: use-pool replenishment (no replenish tag exists at all despite the regex hint) and the 'offering'/'resource' use-types missing from uses/starting; activate-another-ability-ignoring-cost (action compression); discard-pile direct play/resolve recursion; forced enemy disengage and enemy cannot-attack/cannot-move debuffs; resource-move-between-investigators; bonded-swap transform.

AMBIGUITIES / POSSIBLE DUPLICATES I could not fully resolve (flagged inline): (1) ChaosEffectTreatModifierAsZero vs existing ChaosEffectIgnoreModifier — may be the same concept (Accursed/Dawn Star); (2) ChaosRevealAndResolveAnotherInstead vs existing ChaosRevealAnotherInstead — depends on whether the existing tag already covers 'search bag for a specific token and resolve it'; (3) AttachEnemyParley is almost certainly redundant with existing AttachEnemy — included only to surface the enemy-attachment cluster, recommend dropping; (4) ActionExtraNextTurn may fold into existing ActionAdditional; (5) Bianca's 'Uses (resources)' and the offering use-type both surface enum gaps but resource-as-uses is rare. Per rubric I did NOT propose tags for obvious-from-text things (has an [action] ability, Fast/Permanent/Exceptional keywords, bonded/researched designations, attack-of-opportunity-waiving on play) and treated 'move damage/horror to enemy or asset' (Stouthearted, Drain Essence, Wrong Place Right Time) as adequately near existing location/move + heal mechanics, though a dedicated 'move-damage-to-enemy' tag could be a future micro-gap if it recurs.</coverageNotes>
</invoke>

proposedTags.rationale: Three cards in this pack increase your maximum hand size, a core enabler of the Harvey Walters big-hand archetype, yet the taxonomy has NO tag for it (only PhaseUpkeepCheckHandSize, a timing point). Vault of Knowledge (60202): "Your maximum hand size is increased by 2." Arcane Enlightenment (60205): "Your maximum hand size is increased by 1." Laboratory Assistant (60212): "Your maximum hand size is increased by 2." The numeric value is an optional filter; the searchable concept is the hand-size buff. The old regex used hand_size_increase, confirming this is a recognized but un-modeled mechanic.

The defining mechanic of this pack: effects whose strength or availability scales with the number of cards in your hand. No existing tag captures "the more cards in hand, the better." Celaeno Fragments (60206): "While you have ...5 or more cards in hand, you get +1 [intellect]." Higher Education (60211): "While you have 5 or more cards in your hand, Higher Education gains..." Extensive Research (60216): "Reduce the cost to play Extensive Research by 1 for each other card in your hand." Farsight (60231): "if you have 8 or more cards in your hand, exhaust Farsight..." Forbidden Tome (60229/60230): "Reduce this ability's cost by 1 action for every 4 cards in your hand." Players deckbuild around this payoff cluster, so it warrants its own searchable tag (old regex: hand_size_dependent).

Extends the EXISTING cost/action.ts enum, which already has CostActionSpendResource but no secret variant. The CostFree file has CostFreeSpendSecret, so the secret resource type is already modeled there — this is the missing parallel for [action]-activated abilities. Encyclopedia (60208): "[action] Exhaust Encyclopedia and spend 1 secret". Feed the Mind (60209): "[action] Exhaust Feed the Mind and spend 1 secret". Forbidden Tome (60210): "[action] Exhaust Forbidden Tome and spend 1 secret". Old regex used cost_action_spend_secret with no backing tag.

Mind over Matter (60226): "Until the end of the round, add your [intellect] to your [combat] and [agility]." This ADDS one stat on top of others; it is distinct from the existing buff/stats-replace.ts (BuffStatsReplace), whose doc explicitly models substitution ("the stat that replaces another stat" / "the stat that is replaced"). Adding-on-top vs replacing is a different deckbuilding effect (you keep both stats), so it belongs as a sibling tag rather than an argument on the replace tag. from = the donor stat (intellect), to = the recipient stat(s).

proposedCompoundTags.conceptDescription: Cards that build or exploit a large hand / extra card draw as a strategic engine: raw card draw, maximum-hand-size increases, and effects that scale with or are gated by hand size. This is the cross-pack 'big hand' / card-advantage archetype that Seeker (and Harvey Walters specifically) decks are built around.
proposedCompoundTags.rationale: These distinct base tags share one searchable archetype: amassing and cashing in a large hand. A player slotting Vault of Knowledge / Laboratory Assistant (hand-size + draw) wants to find the hand-size payoffs (Higher Education, Celaeno Fragments, Extensive Research, Farsight) and vice versa. Grouping draw, hand-size-increase, and hand-size-dependent lets the synthesis surface the whole engine as one deckbuilding package. har is the seed pack for this archetype; later packs (e.g. additional Seeker support) will extend it.

archetypes.name: Big-Hand / Card-Advantage Engine (Harvey Walters Seeker)
archetypes.description: Increase maximum hand size and draw aggressively, then convert a large hand into stat boosts, cheap plays, and tempo. Splits into enablers (hand-size increase + draw: Vault of Knowledge, Laboratory Assistant, Arcane Enlightenment, Glimpse the Unthinkable, Preposterous Sketches, Feed the Mind) and payoffs that scale with hand size (Higher Education, Celaeno Fragments, Extensive Research, Cryptic Writings's bonus tier, Farsight, Forbidden Tome action discounts).

archetypes.name: Secret-Powered Tome Toolbox
archetypes.description: Tome assets with a (secrets) uses pool spent via [action] or [free] abilities to draw, boost skill value, discover clues, deal damage, or move. Recurring engine across Mystic/Seeker. Needs the CostActionSpendSecret tag to be fully expressible alongside the existing CostFreeSpendSecret and uses-secret tags.

archetypes.name: Intellect-As-Attack / Stat Substitution
archetypes.description: Seeker combat tech: perform a Fight using [intellect] instead of [combat], optionally pumping damage from a resource (cards discarded, clues held). Reuses BuffStatsReplace plus damage-plus and intellect boosts; no new tag strictly required but flagged for verification.

coverageNotes:
Pack 'har' is the Harvey Walters / Miskatonic Seeker set (codes 60202-60233; 31 cards including several upgrade duplicates by name: Whitton Greene 60213/60223, Cryptic Writings 60215/60224, Forbidden Tome 60210/60229/60230).

WELL COVERED by existing taxonomy (do NOT re-propose): card draw (DeckDraw.You/Investigator with value, e.g. 60209/60212/60221/60228/60233); deck search + shuffle for a trait, then draw to hand (DeckSearch.You + DeckShuffle.Player + DiscardPile/PlayArea... actually to-hand via search; Whitton Greene 60213/60223 with trait-relic/trait-tome support tags); clue discovery incl. testless and connecting/any-location (ClueDiscover*, TestlessClue, ClueAdditional, covered by compound clue-tech: 60216/60219/60227/60230/60233); resource gain (GainResource.You with value: 60214/60215/60224); secret uses pools (UsesStarting/UsesSupportSecret: 60208-60210/60233); skill boosts passive & in-test incl. +intellect/+willpower and 'any' (StatsModBoostPassive/InTest: 60206/60208/60211/60233); succeed-by scaling (SkillValueSucceedBy* + test/result, compound succeed-by: 60209/60228); cost structures (CostActionExhaustSelf, CostReactionExhaustSelf, CostFastExhaustSelf, CostFreeSpendResource/Secret, CostDiscount with amount for Library Docent's -2: 60220, reduce-cost handled via CostDiscount); slots (SlotAdditional.Hand/Ally: 60205/60232); permanent/limit handled outside this gap analysis; damage-plus with value (60217/60225); move investigator self (60222/60230); damage relocation (LocationMove.Damage: 60229); damage/horror assignment limit on assets (60232 -> need to confirm a 'damage-limit/horror-limit' tag exists; I did NOT find one in the digest, but it is outside this pack's central archetype and only appears once, so I conservatively did NOT propose it here — flag for a defensive pack synthesis); timing triggers (TimingAfter/When/During/Forced and reaction costs all present).

GAPS PROPOSED: (1) maximum-hand-size increase, (2) hand-size-dependent payoff, (3) cost-action-spend-secret (parallel to the existing cost-free-spend-secret), (4) stats-add (add-on-top, distinct from stats-replace). Plus one compound 'card-advantage-engine'.

AMBIGUITIES / FLAGS: 
- 'uses [intellect] instead of [combat]' (Occult Invocation 60217, \"I've got a plan!\" 60225): I judged this COVERED by buff/stats-replace.ts (from=intellect, to=combat) and did NOT propose a new tag, but note these are one-shot per-attack substitutions tied to a Fight, whereas BuffStatsReplace reads as a passive replacement — confirm the existing tag's intended scope. If it is passive-only, a 'stat-substitute-in-test' variant would be the right addition.
- 'Play an event/asset from hand' as an extra/out-of-sequence play: Farsight (60231) \"Play an event from your hand (paying its cost)\" and Library Docent (60220) \"Play a different Tome asset from your hand\" and Cryptic Writings (60215/60224) \"After you draw... Play it.\" The digest has NO play-from-hand / extra-play / play-when-drawn tag (PlayArea only models ToHand/ToDeck, i.e. returning cards). The old regex used to_play_from_hand and self_play_from_hand. I did NOT propose this because it spans three different sub-mechanics (extra event plays, cost-reduced replay, plays-itself-on-draw) and may be a deliberate omission as 'obvious from text'; recommend the global synthesis decide whether an 'extra-play' archetype is worth one or more tags, since Farsight-style extra-play engines recur in later Seeker/Rogue packs.
- Forbidden Tome 60210 'unidentified/translated' campaign-log mechanic and 60229/60230 'Researched' upgrades are campaign-specific flavor, not searchable game effects — correctly untagged.

proposedTags.rationale: A built-in conditional self-penalty triggered by a BAD chaos token during the card's own action (not a cost paid to activate). Azure Flame (60407): "If an [elder_sign], \"+1,\" or \"0\" token is revealed during this attack, take 1 damage." Clairvoyance (60408/60426/60431): "...take 1 horror." Ineffable Truth (60409/60427/60432): "...lose 1 resource." Astral Travel (60413): "...you must discard an [[Item]] or [[Ally]] asset you control (if you cannot, take 1 damage)." The existing CostFree/CostReactionDamageSelf and CostDamageSelf are COSTS to activate; this is a probabilistic drawback resolved mid-effect. The maintained core source explicitly flags this: rcore.ts line 1016 `// Take horror when revealing chaos tokens - Need new tag type`. The OLD regex used non-existent tags take_damage / take_horror. value = penalty amount; the resource-loss variant is the Ineffable line.

"Max 1 committed per skill test" — a deckbuilding-relevant restriction on a skill card. Guts (60424) and Prescient (60419) both open with "Max 1 committed per skill test." This is a recurring skill-card stamp (Guts/Overpower/Unexpected Courage family). The maintained core source already flags the gap: rcore.ts has `// max_1_commit - Need tag type` on multiple Guts entries. OLD regex used max_1_commit which has no taxonomy entry. value carries the limit (almost always 1).

Uses that automatically refill each round, distinguishing a renewable resource battery from a one-shot Uses pool. Arcane Studies (60428): "Uses (2 resources). Replenish these resources at the start of each round." No existing tag captures replenishment; UsesStarting only records the initial count. OLD regex emitted uses_replenish, which is absent from the taxonomy.

Argument-style extension of the EXISTING UsesStarting enum, which currently has ammo/charge/supply/secret/evidence but no 'resource' variant. Arcane Studies (60428): "Uses (2 resources)." The card stores resources as its Uses pool; the searchable thing (this asset starts with N uses of type resource) already has a home in tags/uses/starting.ts and just needs the missing token type added.

args.name: range
args.type: { type: "top"; cards: number } (reuse DeckSearch range shape)

proposedTags.rationale: Look at the top N cards of the ENCOUNTER deck for information / reordering WITHOUT searching for a specific card to take. Parallel Fates (60415): "Look at the top 4 cards of the encounter deck. ... return them to the top of the encounter deck in any order." DeckSearchEncounter implies pulling a card out; pure scry-and-reorder is a distinct 'encounter deck control / Scrying' archetype. The maintained core source flags it: rcore.ts has `// look_at_encounter - Need tag type` on Scrying (01561) and a similar marker on the 01571 Scrying-like card. Recurring archetype (Scrying, No Stone Unturned, Seeking Answers, Premonition family).

Add charges/uses to a charge-using asset already in play (refuel), enabling a spell/relic to be reused. Recharge (60429): "...add 1 charge to the chosen asset. Otherwise, add 4 charges to the chosen asset." No existing tag covers adding uses to an in-play asset (UsesStarting is the printed amount; UsesSupport is place/move of supports). Searchable as a deck engine piece for charge-hungry Mystic builds. Recurring archetype (Recharge, Enraptured, Practice Makes Perfect-style refuel).

Resolve a chaos-token-triggered effect on one of your cards an ADDITIONAL time (double it), or cancel it. Eldritch Inspiration (60420): "Play when you would resolve an effect on a [mystic] card that triggers \"when,\" \"if,\" or \"after\" a chaos token is revealed. Either cancel that effect, or resolve it an additional time." The cancel half is covered by CancelChaos, but "resolve it an additional time" (effect doubling) has no tag. Sits beside the existing ChaosEffectResolveChoose in tags/chaos/effect.ts.

Name/predict a token type, parity, or test margin, then get a payoff if a matching token was revealed during the test. Crystal Pendulum (60411): "Name a number. If this test succeeds by that number or fails by that number, draw 1 card." Prescient (60419): "name \"even,\" \"odd,\" or \"symbol.\" After this test ends, if a chaos token of the named type was revealed during this test, you may return a [[Spell]] card..." This 'predict the bag' mechanic is its own searchable Jacqueline/Mystic archetype and is not expressible by any chaos-reveal or skill-value tag.

proposedCompoundTags.conceptDescription: Cards that manipulate which chaos tokens get revealed/resolved during a skill test: reveal extra and choose, ignore a symbol's effect/modifier, peek before committing, reveal-before, double or cancel a token-triggered effect. The umbrella players search when building bag-manipulation / Mystic decks.
proposedCompoundTags.rationale: JAC is a dense bag-control pack: Dark Prophecy (60417) reveal 5 choose one (ChaosRevealMore + ResolveChoose), Grotesque Statue (60421) reveal 2 choose one, Defiance (60418) ignore a symbol's effect+modifier before reveal (the identical DWL Defiance 02190 is tagged chaos_ignore_effect/chaos_ignore_modifier/chaos_reveal_before_effect), Scrying Mirror (60406) peek the token before committing cards, Eldritch Inspiration (60420) cancel-or-double a token-triggered effect, Crystal Pendulum/Prescient predict the bag. These distinct base tags share one archetype players search together; no existing compound groups them.

proposedCompoundTags.conceptDescription: Reveal random chaos token(s) from the bag OUTSIDE a skill test as a randomizer/payoff, branching the effect on whether a bad symbol shows. The 'gamble with the bag' archetype (Olive McBride / Voice of Ra family).
proposedCompoundTags.rationale: Voice of Ra (60416): "Reveal 3 random tokens from the chaos bag. For each [skull]/[cultist]/[tablet]/[elder_thing]/[auto_fail] symbol revealed, gain an additional 2 resources." Astral Travel (60413), Recharge (60429), Parallel Fates (60415), Hypnotic Gaze (60414/60423) all reveal token(s) outside a test and branch on the symbol. NOTE: this effect IS expressible via the existing ChaosRevealManual tag (the OLD regex applied chaos_reveal_manual to the identical DWL Hypnotic Gaze 02153 and PTC Recharge 03197 but FAILED to apply it to these JAC cards). I propose only the COMPOUND grouping of ChaosRevealManual + the token tags, since no compound currently names this 'gamble payoff' archetype.

proposedCompoundTags.conceptDescription: Cards that self-inflict a penalty (damage / horror / resource loss) when a bad chaos token is revealed during their own effect — the classic 'risky Mystic spell' drawback.
proposedCompoundTags.rationale: The signature Mystic spell tension: Azure Flame (60407) take 1 damage, Clairvoyance (60408) take 1 horror, Ineffable Truth (60409) lose 1 resource, Astral Travel (60413) discard an asset or take 1 damage — all triggered by an [elder_sign]/+1/0 or a bad symbol. Grouping the proposed downside tags lets players find/avoid self-harm spells as one archetype.

archetypes.name: Bag manipulation (chaos-token control)
archetypes.description: Reveal-extra-and-choose, ignore-symbol, peek-before-committing, double/cancel token effects. Largest theme of the pack; covered mostly by existing chaos/* tags plus the proposed ChaosEffectResolveAdditional and ChaosPredictRevealed.

archetypes.name: Gamble payload (reveal tokens outside a test)
archetypes.description: Reveal random token(s) as a randomizer for a non-test payoff and branch on bad symbols. Expressible via existing ChaosRevealManual + token tags; needs only a compound to name it.

archetypes.name: Risky Mystic spells (willpower-as-X attack/investigate/evade with chaos downside)
archetypes.description: Azure Flame / Clairvoyance / Ineffable Truth: replace a stat with willpower (BuffStatsReplace, covered), get a willpower boost (covered), succeed-payoff (covered), and self-harm on a bad token (the proposed downside tags).

archetypes.name: Predict-the-bag payoff
archetypes.description: Name a number/parity/symbol, then reward if a matching token was revealed (Crystal Pendulum, Prescient). Needs the proposed ChaosPredictRevealed tag.

archetypes.name: Mystic asset economy (charges, replenish, recharge, spell cost reduction)
archetypes.description: Charge-using assets plus refuel and discount enablers: Arcane Studies replenish (proposed UsesReplenish + UsesStartingResource), Recharge refuel (proposed UsesRechargeAsset), Robes of Endless Night spell discount (CostDiscount, covered).

coverageNotes:
Analyzed all 33 cards (codes 60402-60432; several are upgrade-level reprints of Azure Flame / Clairvoyance / Ineffable Truth / Robes / Hypnotic Gaze, so ~16 distinct cards).

ALREADY WELL COVERED by existing taxonomy (do NOT re-propose):
- Per-token-symbol matching during or outside a test: ChaosRevealToken{Skull,Cultist,Tablet,ElderThing,AutoFail,ElderSign} (Azure Flame, Ritual Candles 60405, all the token-checking cards).
- 'Reveal a random token from the chaos bag outside a skill test': ChaosRevealManual already exists and is the correct tag (confirmed by identical cards in dwl.json Hypnotic Gaze 02153 and ptc.json Recharge 03197). The JAC pack JSON simply FAILED to emit chaos_reveal_manual for 60413/60414/60415/60416/60423/60429 — an application gap, not a taxonomy gap.
- Reveal-more-and-choose / ignore-a-symbol / reveal-before: Dark Prophecy 60417 and Grotesque Statue 60421 -> ChaosRevealMore + ChaosEffectResolveChoose (matches core Grotesque Statue 01571). Defiance 60418 -> ChaosEffectIgnoreEffect + ChaosEffectIgnoreModifier + ChaosEffectRevealBeforeEffect (the identical DWL Defiance 02190 carries exactly these; JAC JSON under-tagged it). Scrying Mirror 60406 'perform reveal step before committing' is essentially ChaosEffectRevealBeforeEffect.
- Use willpower instead of combat/intellect/agility: BuffStatsReplace (from/to). Willpower boosts: StatsModBoostInTest/Passive. Extra clue on success: ClueAdditionalThisLocation. Cancel an attack: CancelAttack. Draw on success: DeckDrawYou. Gain resources: GainResourceYou. Cost reduction of a Spell: CostDiscount. Additional arcane slot: SlotAdditionalArcane (the Spell-only restriction on Familiar Spirit 60410 is a minor un-captured nuance). Exhaust-to-activate reaction costs: CostReactionExhaustSelf. Deck restriction (Arbiter 60402): DeckRestriction. Return a Spell from discard to hand (Prescient): DiscardPileToHand. Uses charge/secret/resource starting counts: UsesStarting* (except the missing 'resource' variant, proposed).

GENUINE GAPS confirmed by `// Need new tag type` markers in the maintained source (tags/src/tagged-cards/rcore.ts): (1) self-damage/horror/resource-loss downside on a bad chaos token [line 1016], (2) 'Max 1 committed per skill test' [multiple Guts entries], (3) 'look at top N of encounter deck' scry [Scrying 01561]. Plus replenishing uses, the UsesStarting 'resource' variant, recharge-an-asset, resolve-a-chaos-effect-an-additional-time (Eldritch Inspiration), and predict-the-bag (Crystal Pendulum/Prescient).

AMBIGUITIES / borderline (left as covered, flagged for synthesis):
- Robes of Endless Night 60422 adds 'Playing that card does not provoke attacks of opportunity' on top of the cost discount — no AoO-suppression tag exists, but it is too niche/rider-like to propose from one card; revisit if it recurs.
- Scrying Mirror 60406 reorders the skill-test STEP sequence (reveal token before committing). Treated as ChaosEffectRevealBeforeEffect; if 'reorder test steps' recurs distinctly it may warrant its own tag.
- The proposed downside tags vs. existing Cost*DamageSelf: I treat the bad-token penalty as a separate 'downside' concept (resolved mid-effect, not a paid activation cost). If the maintainer prefers, DownsideTakeDamage/Horror could instead be folded as a chaos-conditional variant under tags/chaos rather than a new 'downside' folder.</coverageNotes>
</invoke>

proposedTags.rationale: Galvanize (60121): "Ready a [guardian] asset you control." No existing tag expresses readying your OWN cards/assets. The only 'ready'-related enum is TagTypeEnemyDebuff.EnemyDoesNotReady (about enemies) and the upkeep PhaseUpkeepReadyCards framework step. Readying-your-own-assets is a recognized recurring deckbuilding archetype (re-using an exhausted weapon/ally/tool a second time in a round) that players actively search for, and nothing here covers it.

One-Two Punch (60117): "If you succeed, you may fight that enemy again." and its upgrade (60132): "You may fight again." This grants an extra ATTACK within the resolution of the current card, NOT a new action — so it is not expressible by TagTypeActionAdditional.ActionAdditional (which grants an action that 'can only be used to fight'; that tag models Galvanize-style extra actions). 'Fight again / attack again' is its own searchable burst-damage archetype. Proposed as a sibling variant in the existing action/additional.ts file.

Mano a Mano (60125): "This action does not provoke attacks of opportunity." Avoiding attacks of opportunity is a discrete, keyword-like benefit players explicitly search for (it changes how safely you can act while engaged), and no existing tag or argument captures it. The old regex hint 'not_aoo' confirms it was being detected but has no home in the taxonomy.

Randall Cho (60102): "search your deck and discard pile for a [[Weapon]] asset, play it (paying its cost), and shuffle your deck." The search itself is covered by TagTypeDeckSearch.DeckSearchYou, but PUTTING THE FOUND CARD DIRECTLY INTO PLAY (bypassing hand) is a distinct 'tutor-into-play / cheat-into-play' archetype with no existing tag. TagTypeDeckSearch has no destination field and assumes search-to-hand (as in Boxing Gloves 60105/60127 which explicitly 'add it to your hand'). The play-from-deck destination is the searchable novelty.

proposedCompoundTags.conceptDescription: Cards whose benefit triggers off defeating an enemy (the kill is the engine): draw cards, discover clues, gain resources, or tutor cards when an enemy dies. A core Guardian/aggro deckbuilding axis — players assemble these together so each kill cascades into card/clue/resource value.
proposedCompoundTags.rationale: Multiple cards here reward the kill rather than the test: Glory (60115) "Play after you defeat an enemy. Draw 2 cards"; Evidence! (60120) "Play after you defeat an enemy. Discover 1 clue..."; Boxing Gloves (60105/60127) "After you defeat an enemy... Search the top N cards..."; Grete Wagner (60107/60128) "After you defeat an enemy... Discover 1 clue". The shared archetype (turn defeats into resources) is broader than any single base tag, so it warrants a compound grouping for 'find similar payoff cards'.

proposedCompoundTags.conceptDescription: Cards that respond to being attacked by an enemy with a defensive AND offensive answer — cancel the incoming attack and/or immediately strike the attacking enemy. Players search these together as an 'enemy-management on the enemy phase' toolkit.
proposedCompoundTags.rationale: Counterpunch (60112/60122) "Play after an enemy attacks you... This attack targets the attacking enemy"; Dodge (60113) "Play when an enemy attacks an investigator at your location. Cancel that attack." These pair offense (strike the attacker) with defense (cancel) keyed off the same enemy-attacks trigger. The existing 'thorns' and 'attack-mitigation' compounds capture parts (retaliation-after-damage, cancel-attack) but not the unified 'respond to the attack declaration with a counter-strike' archetype.

archetypes.name: Defeat-enemy value engine
archetypes.description: Aggressive Guardian package where defeating an enemy is the trigger for card draw, clue discovery, resource gain, or tutoring. Cards are intentionally cheap/fast so the kill cascades into tempo. Recurs widely beyond this pack (e.g. various 'after you defeat an enemy' assets/events).

archetypes.name: Pull-and-punch (enemy relocation + forced fight)
archetypes.description: Drag a distant enemy to your location, engage it, and attack it in one action — converting positioning into immediate combat. Covered today by LocationMoveEnemyToYou + EnemyEngageEnemy + ActionBoldFight, but flagged as a coherent archetype for synthesis.

archetypes.name: Resource 'big money' / pseudo-economy off combat
archetypes.description: Generating resources as a side-effect of fighting or defeating enemies, rather than from dedicated economy cards: gain resources when a Fight action begins, store excess damage and cash it in, or share resources with allies. First seeds here of a combat-funded economy archetype.

archetypes.name: Counter-attack / retaliation toolkit
archetypes.description: Reactive enemy-phase answers that cancel an incoming attack and/or strike the attacking enemy. Pairs with the existing 'thorns' and 'attack-mitigation' compounds but emphasizes the proactive counter-strike on attack declaration.

archetypes.name: Extra-attack damage burst
archetypes.description: Single events that grant a follow-up attack with stacked combat/damage bonuses (and sometimes auto-success), front-loading burst damage into one action. Drives the proposed ActionAdditionalAttack tag.

coverageNotes:
This is the Nathaniel Cho starter (pack 'nat', Guardian; 31 cards including level-0 and upgraded versions). The existing taxonomy already covers the bulk of these cards well: combat/willpower stat boosts in-test and passive (StatsModBoostInTest/Passive incl. the 'while fighting' qualifier and 'spend resource' pumps), damage bonuses (DamagePlus value 1/2), testless damage at your/connecting/attacking-enemy locations (TestlessDamage*), testless clues + clue discovery at your/connecting locations (ClueDiscover*, TestlessClue), card draw (DeckDrawYou value), deck search top-N with shuffle (DeckSearchYou range:top:N + DeckShufflePlayer), heal damage (HealDamageYou), resource gain you/investigator (GainResource*), cancel attack/damage/horror (Cancel*), enemy relocation + engage + fight (LocationMoveEnemyToYou, EnemyEngageEnemy, ActionBold*), additional ACTION restricted to fight (ActionAdditional with canOnlyBeUsedTo), uses/charges/resources (Uses*), all the cost tags (free/fast/reaction spend/exhaust/damage-self), elite-unusable (EnemyEliteNonEliteOnly), max-1-committed and succeed-by margins (SkillValue*/TestResult), AutoSuccess, first-action and timing windows (Timing*), and the not-aoo-adjacent thorns/attack-mitigation compounds.
