args.name: from
args.type: SkillType (the stat normally used, e.g. agility/combat)

args.name: to
args.type: SkillType (the stat used instead, e.g. willpower/intellect)

args.name: action
args.type: TestingBasicAction? (fight | evade | investigate — the action whose test the substitution applies to)

args.name: mode
args.type: "instead" | "add" ("instead" = use X instead of Y; "add" = add X to skill value in addition)

proposedTags.rationale: Many tfa cards swap or add a stat for a single action's test, e.g. Mists of R'lyeh (04029): "This evasion attempt uses [willpower] instead of [agility]"; Ornate Bow (04204): "This attack uses [agility] instead of [combat]"; Blood Eclipse (04266): "This attack uses [willpower] instead of [combat]"; Slip Away (04232): "Add your [intellect] to your skill value for this evasion attempt"; Timeworn Brand (04276): "Add your [willpower] to your skill value for this attack." The existing TagBuffStatsReplace (from/to) is a PERMANENT passive replacement of a stat (Mr. Rook style), with no notion of a per-test scope or the action context (fight/evade/investigate) that makes these cards searchable. This is one of the most recurring deckbuilding archetypes (off-stat fighters/evaders) and is the single biggest gap in this pack. The old regex hints (stat_use_willpower, stat_not_agility, stat_add_intellect_for_evade) confirm the concept but the taxonomy cannot express it.

Two tfa cards force the end of your turn as a tradeoff for a powerful effect, a distinct cost/drawback players search for. Pay Day (04233): "If it is your turn, end your turn." and Coup de Grâce (04269): "...draw 1 card. If it is your turn, end your turn." No existing tag expresses ending your turn (ActionLoseAction is losing a single action, not ending the turn; the duration tags are about effect duration, not the turn-ending consequence). Recurring across packs (Ace in the Hole, etc.).

args.name: shuffleBack
args.type: boolean (true if it shuffles itself back into the deck after resolving, the Survivor 'recur forever' pattern)

proposedTags.rationale: A recurring Survivor archetype: the card may be played from your own discard pile (paying its cost), then often shuffles itself back. Improvised Weapon (04033): "You may play Improvised Weapon from your discard pile. If you do, shuffle it into your deck after resolving its effects."; Winging It (04272) and Impromptu Barrier (04312) share the identical template. The existing recursion-event/recursion-asset/recursion-skill tags describe returning OTHER cards to hand; they have no field for a card that replays ITSELF from the discard pile, which is the searchable property here (discard-pile value, fewer copies needed).

args.name: value
args.type: number (total damage that may be distributed; use -1 for X)

proposedTags.rationale: Flamethrower (04305): "instead of its standard damage, you may assign up to 4 damage among enemies engaged with you (any additional damage adds to this total)." This area/spread-damage attack is distinct from DamagePlus (a flat bonus to one target) and from the testless damage tags — the searchable property is hitting multiple enemies at once. First-of-archetype for group-clear weapons.

args.name: condition
args.type: string? (e.g. evade value threshold, succeed-by based)

proposedTags.rationale: Impromptu Barrier (04312): "you may evade an additional enemy at the same location with evade X or lower." Evading more than one enemy with a single action is a distinct evasion-package property with no existing tag (the testless-evade and bold-evade tags do not capture multi-target evasion). Pairs with the multi-target damage tag for an 'AoE control' archetype.

proposedCompoundTags.conceptDescription: Cards that manipulate the chaos bag / chaos-token reveal step: revealing extra tokens and choosing among them, ignoring or cancelling bad symbols, not revealing tokens at all, sealing tokens away, or pre-committing to / checking which token is revealed. The flagship Mystic/token-manipulation deckbuilding package players search as one group.
proposedCompoundTags.rationale: tfa is saturated with chaos-bag tech that players unambiguously search as one archetype, but no compound currently groups it. Reveal-more: Olive McBride (04197) "Reveal 3 chaos tokens instead of 1", Dark Prophecy (04032), Against All Odds (04202). Ignore: Defiance (04198) "Ignore the effects of all [skull], [cultist], [tablet], and [elder_thing] symbols". Cancel: Counterspell (04110) "Cancel that chaos token." Do-not-reveal: Pnakotic Manuscripts (04307) "Do not reveal chaos tokens for that test." Seal/pre-set: Premonition (04199), The Codex of Ages (04013), The Chthonian Stone (04030), Protective Incantation (04031), Crystalline Elder Sign (04235). Check-what-is-revealed: Recall the Future (04158). This is the canonical cross-pack 'chaos-token control' grouping the rubric calls out.

proposedCompoundTags.conceptDescription: Cards whose payoff is generating resources (economy / 'big money'), grouping the existing gain-resource tags so players can find money engines and burst-income cards together.
proposedCompoundTags.rationale: tfa has a cluster of resource-economy cards that players deckbuild around together but which currently only carry the atomic gain-resource-* tags with no archetype grouping: Pay Day (04233) "Gain 1 resource for each action you performed this turn", High Roller (04156) "If you succeed, gain 3 resources", Decorated Skull (04026) "...gain 1 resource", Take Heart (04201) "...gains 2 resources", "You handle this one!" (04028) "Gain 1 resource". Naming this archetype lets a later global synthesis collect the 'big-money' package.

proposedCompoundTags.conceptDescription: Cards whose payoff is drawing extra cards (card-advantage engines), grouping the draw tags so players can find card-draw economy as one searchable archetype.
proposedCompoundTags.rationale: Numerous tfa cards center on repeatable or burst card draw — an archetype players assemble deliberately: Lucky Cigarette Case (04107) "...Draw 1 card" on every big success, Tooth of Eztli (04023), Decorated Skull (04026) "Draw 1 card", Feed the Mind (04267) "For each point you succeed by, draw 1 card", All In (04309) "draw 1 card for each point you succeeded by, to a maximum of 5", Take Heart (04201) "draws 2 cards". Currently only atomic draw-player-N tags exist with no archetype-level grouping.

proposedCompoundTags.conceptDescription: Cards that let you perform an action's skill test with a different stat than normal (use X instead of Y, or add X to skill value) — the 'off-stat fighter/evader/investigator' package built around the proposed StatSubstituteInTest tag plus related off-stat boosts.
proposedCompoundTags.rationale: A recurring deckbuilding identity is fighting or evading with an off-stat (e.g. willpower-based combat for Mystics, intellect-based evasion). tfa supplies Mists of R'lyeh (04029/04271, evade with willpower), Ornate Bow (04204, fight with agility), Blood Eclipse (04266, fight with willpower), Handcuffs (04265, evade with combat), Shards of the Void (04310, fight with willpower), Slip Away (04232, add intellect to evade), Timeworn Brand (04276, add willpower to attack). Grouping the per-test substitution tag with the permanent BuffStatsReplace lets players find the whole off-stat package; it depends on the proposed StatSubstituteInTest base tag.

archetypes.name: Chaos-token control (bag manipulation)
archetypes.description: The Mystic/token-tech package: reveal extra tokens and pick, ignore/cancel bad symbols, do-not-reveal, seal tokens, and check/pre-set what is revealed. tfa is one of the densest packs for this. Captured by the proposed chaos-token-control compound over existing chaos/* and cancel-chaos tags.

archetypes.name: Off-stat fighting / evading
archetypes.description: Perform fight/evade/investigate tests with a substituted or added stat (willpower-combat, agility-combat, intellect-evade, etc.). The pack's biggest taxonomy gap; needs the proposed StatSubstituteInTest tag and off-stat-action compound.

archetypes.name: Discard-pile recursion (self-replaying events)
archetypes.description: Survivor events that play from the discard pile and shuffle themselves back, giving near-unlimited reuse. Needs the proposed RecursionSelfFromDiscard tag.

archetypes.name: Resource economy / big money
archetypes.description: Cards that generate bursts or streams of resources to fuel expensive plays. Grouped by the proposed resource-generation compound.

archetypes.name: Card-draw economy
archetypes.description: Cards built to draw extra cards, often scaling with success margin. Grouped by the proposed card-draw-engine compound.

archetypes.name: Researched / campaign-evolving upgrades
archetypes.description: The 'Unidentified -> Researched' mechanic (Ancient Stone variants) and supporting upgrade tech (Shrewd Analysis). Currently only loosely captured by the 'researched' regex hint; the upgrade-cost-reduction effects (Arcane Research) are intentionally campaign-log/deckbuilding and largely outside the in-game-effect taxonomy. Flagged as an ambiguity rather than a firm proposal.

coverageNotes:
Pack contains 76 player cards (codes 04006-04312). The existing taxonomy already covers the bulk of tfa well, so the true gap is small and concentrated:

WELL COVERED (do not re-propose): weapon attacks with combat/agility boosts and damage-plus (boost-in-test, damage-plus); uses & charges/ammo/supply/secret economy (uses-starting, uses-support place/move covers Venturer 04018, Truth from Fiction 04152, Custom Ammunition 04193, Enraptured 04157); fight/evade/investigate/parley action designators (action-bold-*); clue discovery and shroud reduction (clue-discover, shroud-*, additional-clue, clue-tech compound); chaos seal and chaos reveal-token symbol tags (every seal/reveal card's tokens are expressible); cancel (Counterspell 04110, Perseverance 04111); heal damage/horror incl. ally/investigator (Thermos 04274, Kerosene 04304, Ancient Stone 04231); deck-restriction (Mitch 04006, etc.); attach asset/enemy/location (Trusted 04019, Handcuffs 04265, Skeleton Key 04270); enemy-to-encounter-deck (Persuasion 04105, Dumb Luck 04034, via enemy-mitigation-back-to-encounter-deck); search/shuffle (Smuggled Goods 04010, Backpack 04037, Dr. Elli 04021); skill-icon commit tricks (Yaotl 04035, Last Chance 04036, Take the Initiative 04150 via skill_icons — note skill_icons itself is a regex hint with no obvious enum in the digest, treated as already-handled); enemy fight/evade reduction (Improvised Weapon 04033, Expose Weakness 04195); does-not-ready debuff (Slip Away 04232, Handcuffs 04265); additional actions (Borrowed Time 04308 is covered by the existing TagActionAdditional with its value field — NOT a gap); not-AoO, fast/free/reaction costs, timing tags.

GENUINE GAPS (proposed above): (1) per-test stat substitution/addition with action context — the single biggest gap, pervasive and cross-pack, not covered by the permanent-only BuffStatsReplace; (2) end-your-turn drawback; (3) self-recursion play-from-discard (distinct from the other-card recursion tags); (4) multi-target/spread damage (Flamethrower); (5) multi-target evade (Impromptu Barrier). Plus four compound tags grouping cross-pack archetypes: chaos-token-control (flagship), resource-generation, card-draw-engine, off-stat-action.

AMBIGUITIES I COULD NOT FULLY RESOLVE: (a) The 'Researched'/'Unidentified' campaign-evolution mechanic and experience-cost-reduction upgrades (Ancient Stone 04022/04230/04231, Shrewd Analysis 04106, Arcane Research 04109) are largely deckbuilding/campaign-log effects rather than in-play game effects; unclear whether the taxonomy intends to tag them at all, so I did not propose a tag and only flag the archetype. (b) Until the End of Time (04015) 'Direct damage and direct horror may be assigned to this' is a damage-soak/redirect mechanic with no matching tag, but it is a single unique investigator-specific card, so I judged it below the threshold for a new tag (flagging it here for the global synthesis in case soak-redirect recurs). (c) Recall the Future (04158) 'name a chaos token ... if revealed, +2' is a 'check what is revealed' effect plausibly belonging in the chaos-token-control compound via the existing chaos-reveal-during-effect regex hint; I included it in the compound's example set but note the underlying base tag mapping is uncertain.</coverageNotes>
</invoke>

args.name: asCost
args.type: boolean (optional) - true when adding is an additional cost / drawback rather than a benefit

proposedTags.rationale: The single biggest gap. The existing chaos taxonomy only covers REVEALING a token type (ChaosRevealTokenBless), SEALING (ChaosSealTokenBless), or token-resolution EFFECTS (ChaosEffect*). It cannot express the core Innsmouth mechanic of ACTIVELY PUTTING bless tokens INTO the chaos bag. The regex slapped 'chaos_reveal_token_bless' on all of these even though no reveal happens. Keep Faith: 'Add 4 [bless] tokens to the chaos bag.' Book of Psalms: 'Add 2 [bless] tokens to the chaos bag.' Hand of Fate: 'add [bless] tokens to the chaos bag equal to the attacking enemy's total combined damage.' Signum Crucis: 'add X [bless] tokens to the chaos bag.' A 'bless deck' player searches for exactly this.

args.name: asCost
args.type: boolean (optional) - true when adding curses is the additional cost/drawback to enable a stronger effect

proposedTags.rationale: Curse counterpart, and frequently the additional-cost 'curse engine' pattern that defines this cycle. Deep Knowledge: 'As an additional cost to play Deep Knowledge, add 2 [curse] tokens to the chaos bag.' Faustian Bargain: 'add 2 [curse] tokens to the chaos bag.' Promise of Power: 'After you commit ... add 1 [curse] token to the chaos bag.' Riastrad: 'add up to 3 [curse] tokens to the chaos bag. For each [curse] token added ... you get +1 [combat].' Stirring Up Trouble / Justify the Means add curses equal to shroud / difficulty. None of this is captured by reveal/seal tags.

Returning/removing bless tokens FROM the bag (the inverse of add) is its own searchable effect, e.g. the cost to power a payoff or to balance the bag. Hallow: 'return a total of 10 [bless] tokens to the token pool from the chaos bag or sealed on cards in play.' A Watchful Peace: 'search the chaos bag and/or cards in play for a total of 5 [bless] tokens and return them to the token pool.' Sacred Covenant returns revealed bless tokens. No existing tag expresses bag depletion.

Curse-removal is a distinct deckbuilding want (curse mitigation / 'I run curses but want to clean the bag'). Harmony Restored: 'Search the chaos bag for X [curse] tokens and return them to the token pool. X is the number of [bless] tokens in the chaos bag.' Predestined: 'remove 2 [curse] tokens from the chaos bag.' Rite of Equilibrium option: 'Remove X [curse] and X [bless] tokens from the chaos bag.' Not expressible today.

Bulk swap of one token type for another IN THE BAG (not a per-test reveal effect). This is a recognizable archetype (bless/curse 'flip the bag'). Tides of Fate: 'Replace all [curse] tokens in the chaos bag with an equal number of [bless] tokens. At the end of the round, replace all [bless] ... with ... [curse].' Cryptic Grimoire: 'Replace 5 [curse] tokens in the chaos bag with 5 [bless] tokens.' Rite of Equilibrium: 'Add X [curse] tokens ... to add X [bless] tokens.' Distinct from per-test ChaosEffectTreatAsElderSign.

args.name: from
args.type: ChaosTokenType — token being converted (e.g. bless, curse)

args.name: to
args.type: ChaosTokenType / 'modifier' — what it becomes during the test

proposedTags.rationale: Existing ChaosEffectTreatAsElderSign covers only the elder-sign case. A whole sub-archetype here converts a REVEALED token into a different one DURING the test. Blessing of Isis: 'Cancel that token and treat it as if it were a [elder_sign] token instead.' Curse of Aeons: 'treat it as if it were a [skull] token instead.' 'Lucky' Penny: 'treat that token as a [bless] token / treat that token as a [curse] token.' Skeptic / Blasphemous Covenant: 'treat the modifier of each [bless] and each [curse] token as +1.' Generalizing the existing elder-sign tag with from/to args would unify these.

ChaosSeal enum has token-0, any, auto-fail, cultist, elder-sign, elder-thing, skull, tablet — but NO bless and NO curse, despite this being the bless/curse pack. Multiple cards search the bag and seal bless tokens on themselves. Radiant Smite: 'search the chaos bag for up to 3 [bless] tokens, and seal them here.' Holy Spear: 'Search the chaos bag for 2 [bless] tokens and seal them on Holy Spear.' Rite of Sanctification / Shield of Faith: 'Seal (up to 5 [bless]).' Nephthys seals bless. This is the most glaring missing enum member in seal.ts.

Curse seal is likewise absent from the ChaosSeal enum. Dark Ritual: 'Seal (up to 5 [curse]).' Flute of the Outer Gods: 'Seal (up to X [curse])' then '[action] ... release 1 [curse] token sealed on it.' Favor of the Moon: 'Seal (up to 3 [curse]).' Unrelenting seals chosen tokens. Needed to mirror ChaosSealTokenBless.

A recurring 'power at the price of doom' cost not covered by cost/* (which only has discard/exhaust/damage/horror/resource/charge/secret). Blood Pact: '[free] Add 1 doom to Blood Pact: You get +2 [willpower].' Abyssal Tome: 'you may place 1 doom on Abyssal Tome (to a maximum of 3). You get +1 skill value ... for each doom.' DoomAdd exists but is generic 'add doom' (e.g. to agenda); this is specifically self-doom as an activation cost, a distinct deckbuilding hazard players filter on.

The 'additional cost: add tokens to the bag' template is a distinct, searchable cost archetype (the curse-tax of this cycle). Deep Knowledge: 'As an additional cost to play Deep Knowledge, add 2 [curse] tokens.' Stirring Up Trouble: 'add [curse] tokens ... equal to your location's shroud value.' Justify the Means: 'add [curse] tokens ... equal to this test's difficulty.' Distinct from ChaosBagAddCurse (which is the effect form); here it is gating play/commit as a cost. Could alternatively be modeled as ChaosBagAddCurse{asCost:true}; flagging both options for the synthesizer.

args.name: canOnlyBeUsedTo
args.type: BasicAction — needs an 'engage' member if not present

proposedTags.rationale: Riot Whistle: 'You may take an additional action during your turn, which can only be used to engage.' This is exactly the existing TagActionAdditional with canOnlyBeUsedTo. NOT a new tag — flagging only to confirm BasicAction enum includes 'engage' so the restriction can be captured. If it already does, this is fully covered and needs no change.

args.name: value
args.type: number — the base skill value it is set to

proposedTags.rationale: SETTING base skill value (not the +N modifiers covered by stats-mod/boost-*) is a distinct effect. Eye of the Djinn: 'Set your base skill value to 5 for this test.' Existing skill-value tags are about test margins; stats-mod tags are additive boosts. Setting/overriding the base value is neither. Niche (1 card here) but the first instance of an archetype worth naming.

Cancelling/suppressing a drawn weakness is a distinct support effect not covered by cancel/* (which has revelation/encounter-draw/encounter-effect but those target encounter cards, not the player weakness mechanic) nor by deck/*. Ikiaq: 'When an investigator at your location draws a basic weakness ... Cancel that weakness's effects and place it facedown beneath Ikiaq.' Recurring archetype (weakness hatebears). One clear instance here.

proposedCompoundTags.conceptDescription: Cards that actively manipulate the contents of the chaos bag with bless/curse tokens — adding, removing/returning, or replacing them — the core engine of a bless or curse deck. This is the 'big knob' players search when building around the [bless]/[curse] subtheme, distinct from per-test reveal effects.
proposedCompoundTags.rationale: Innsmouth introduced bless/curse as a token-economy. Players ask 'what fills my bag with bless?' or 'what cleans curses?' across the whole game, not pack by pack. Keep Faith (add bless), Tempt Fate (add both), Harmony Restored (remove curse), Tides of Fate (replace curse->bless). Grouping the add/remove/replace base tags lets the synthesis surface the entire bag-control package.

proposedCompoundTags.conceptDescription: Cards that REWARD bless tokens being in the bag / revealed: extra damage, extra clues, draw, healing, or auto-success when bless/elder-sign tokens appear. The payoff half of a bless deck (the engine half is bless-curse-bag-control).
proposedCompoundTags.rationale: Bless decks pair a token-source with payoffs that key off bless. Blessed Blade ('If a [bless] or [elder_sign] token is revealed ... deals +1 damage'), Radiant Smite (seal bless for +damage), Jacob Morrison (ready on bless reveal), Beloved (bless -> auto-success). Distinct from merely adding tokens; this is the value side players match against their token source.

proposedCompoundTags.conceptDescription: Cards that reward curse/auto-fail tokens being revealed — bonus damage, clues, charges, resources, or extra actions triggered by [curse] or [auto_fail] reveals. The payoff half of a curse deck.
proposedCompoundTags.rationale: Curse decks accept a worse bag in exchange for payoffs that trigger on curse reveals. Armageddon ('If a [curse] token is revealed ... deal 1 damage or place 1 charge'), Eye of Chaos, Shroud of Shadows, Gaze of Ouraxsh ('1 additional damage for each [curse] or [auto_fail] token revealed'), Cryptic Grimoire ('After you resolve 1 or more [curse] tokens ... Place that many secrets'). Mirror of bless-payoff.

coverageNotes:
Pack 'tic' = The Innsmouth Conspiracy player set (cycle 07), the bless/curse cycle. 75 cards analyzed (some duplicate names are distinct upgrade/researched versions, e.g. three Cryptic Grimoires 07022/07191/07192, two Armageddons, two Eye of Chaos, two Shroud of Shadows, two .25 Automatics — each counted separately).

ALREADY WELL COVERED (do not re-propose): bold actions (fight/evade/investigate/engage/move), stat boosts in-test and passive (boost_*; Keen Eye, Blood Pact, Hyperawareness family), damage-plus (Sea Change Harpoon, Holy Spear), uses/starting + uses/replenish + uses/support (charges/ammo/secrets/offerings; Eldritch Sophist, Ariadne's Twine move-secret), cost-action/fast/free/reaction families (exhaust-self, spend-resource, discard-self, damage-self, horror-self), deck-restriction (Sister Mary/Amanda/Trish/Dexter/Silas signature cards), fast_play + timing-fast-during-your-turn, buff-stats-replace (willpower-substitution: Sword Cane, Armageddon, Eye of Chaos, Shroud of Shadows, Abyssal Tome), succeed-by (Breaking and Entering), cancel-attack (Obfuscation, Hand of Fate, Shield of Faith), discard-zero-uses, draw (Plan of Action, Tempt Fate, Unrelenting), gain-resource (Harmony Restored, Favor of the Moon), heal (Book of Psalms, Manipulate Destiny, Spirit of Humanity), shroud +/- (Cryptographic Cipher), additional-clue / discover-clue (Eye of Chaos, Stirring Up Trouble, Mariner's Compass), max-1-commit / limit-1-per-deck, trait_covenant/insight/relic/weapon/ally, recursion (Shrine of the Moirai returns cards from discard — covered by discard-pile-to-hand), elite-unusable, location-move-enemy (Flute, Shroud of Shadows), testless damage (Gaze of Ouraxsh, Manipulate Destiny), heal-via-token reveal.

THE REAL GAP is chaos-bag CONTENT manipulation. The taxonomy can express revealing a token TYPE, sealing a (limited set of) token types, and per-resolution chaos EFFECTS — but it has NO way to express ADD / REMOVE-RETURN / REPLACE bless or curse tokens in the bag, which is THE defining mechanic of this entire cycle and recurs on ~25 cards. The old regex tag 'chaos_reveal_token_bless/curse' was blanket-applied to add/remove/seal/reveal indiscriminately, masking the gap — it should NOT be trusted as evidence of coverage. Also missing: ChaosSeal enum lacks bless AND curse members (the pack's namesake tokens). Secondary smaller gaps: self-doom-as-cost (Blood Pact, Abyssal Tome), additional-cost-add-tokens (Deep Knowledge, Stirring Up Trouble, Justify the Means), treat-revealed-token-as-X beyond elder-sign, set-base-skill-value (Eye of the Djinn), weakness-draw-cancel (Ikiaq).

AMBIGUITIES / JUDGMENT CALLS FLAGGED FOR SYNTHESIS: (1) Whether 'additional cost: add curse tokens' should be its own cost tag (CostAddChaosTokenToPlay) or just ChaosBagAddCurse with an asCost flag — I propose the flag approach as primary but list both. (2) Riot Whistle's engage-only extra action is fully expressible by existing TagActionAdditional IF BasicAction includes 'engage'; could not confirm the BasicAction enum membership from the digest (kohaku.js not shown) — no new tag if it does. (3) Cards that 'search the chaos bag and seal' (Radiant Smite, Holy Spear, Unrelenting, Nephthys) combine a search + seal; I treat them as ChaosSealTokenBless/Curse rather than DeckSearch (which is deck-scoped). (4) 'Treat modifier as +1' (Skeptic, Blasphemous Covenant) sits between ChaosEffectModifier and the proposed ChaosEffectTreatTokenAs; I grouped under treat-token-as but it may warrant ChaosEffectModifier reuse. (5) Permanent Covenants are mechanically covered but form a tight sub-archetype worth surfacing. (6) Eye of the Djinn 'set base skill value to 5' is genuinely novel vs all boost/skill-value tags. (7) Enchanted Armor (07189) and Under Surveillance (07157) are mostly encounter-interaction utility with thin player-mechanic content; Enchanted Armor's self-test-on-damage and Under Surveillance's auto-evade-on-spawn are edge cases I did not propose tags for (one-offs, low search value).</coverageNotes>

proposedTags.rationale: Several TSK skill cards exist specifically to commit to a DIFFERENT investigator's test, and/or to commit at a distance — a distinct, searchable 'committer / Carson Sinclair support' archetype with no existing tag. The taxonomy only has TimingSkillSt2CommitCards (a framework timing point) and TestYouPerform (the opposite). 09002 '"As you wish"': 'Commit only to a skill test being performed by another investigator.' 09030 Fighting Lessons: 'You can commit this skill to an investigator's test at any location.' 09032 Bestow Resolve: 'spend 1 charge: Commit a non-weakness card from your hand to that skill test' of an investigator 'at your location or a connecting location'. The optional range arg captures the searchable filter (remote vs local).

A signature TSK engine: place resources from the token pool onto THIS card as a renamed, self-growing counter via a reaction/effect, then spend them later. This is NOT a printed 'Uses (N x)' pool (UsesStarting) nor a place/move of an existing use type (UsesSupport) — it is an accumulator that starts empty and grows. 09016 Darrell's Kodak: 'Place 1 resource (from the token pool) on that enemy or treachery, as evidence.' 09043 Dissection Tools: 'Place 1 resource (from the token pool) on this card, as evidence.' 09045 Research Notes: 'Place that many resources on Research Notes, as evidence.' 09102 Soul Sanctification: 'place 1 resource on Soul Sanctification, as an offering.' Also 09026 Breach the Door ('1 resource on it ... as leads').

A recurring 'encounter-deck filtering / soft-cancel' effect distinct from the existing CancelEncounterDraw (which removes the card entirely): draw/reveal MORE encounter cards and choose which to resolve, discarding the rest. Players search this as encounter mitigation. 09054 Dr. William T. Maleson: 'That investigator draws another card from the top of the encounter deck, chooses one of those 2 cards to resolve, and cancels and discards the other.' 09111 Nature of the Beast: 'Reveal the top 3 cards of the encounter deck. Choose an investigator to draw 1 of the revealed cards and discard the rest.' This is a meaningfully different, searchable tech than full cancellation.

proposedCompoundTags.conceptDescription: Cards that deliberately place doom on a card you control as a powerful resource, then remove that doom as the payoff loop — a self-contained doom-acceleration engine that players build around (and pair with doom-removal tech).
proposedCompoundTags.rationale: A defining TSK (mystic) archetype: pay power with doom, then scrub it. 09082/09096 Ceremonial Sickle: 'place 1 doom on it to get +... and deal +1 damage' / 'remove 1 doom'. 09083/09097 Dowsing Rod and 09085/09098 Onyx Pentacle share the identical 'place 1 doom to overcharge / remove doom on a condition' template. 09093 Moonlight Ritual: 'Remove all doom from a non-Elite card at your location.' 09094 Sin-Eater and 09092 Elle Rubash manage doom on your own assets. Base tags doom-add/doom-remove exist but the searchable thing is the combined self-doom engine; a compound makes it findable as a deckbuilding package.

archetypes.name: Committer / remote skill-test support

Pairs with the existing 'support' compound but the commit-to-others mechanic itself is currently untagged.

archetypes.description: Place doom on your own asset to overcharge an action, then remove that doom on a success condition; supported by dedicated doom-scrubbing cards.

Many overlap existing attach-enemy / enemy-debuff tags but several effects (exhaust-on-move, 'cannot take damage', 'gains aloof', 'doom cannot be placed') are not individually tagged.

coverageNotes: Analyzed all 118 cards in tsk.json (codes 09002-09123). EXISTING TAXONOMY ALREADY COVERS WELL (verified, do NOT treat as gaps): bold actions (fight/evade/investigate/parley) on Bonesaw, Runic Axe, Grim Memoir, Map the Area, Onyx Pentacle, etc.; in-test stat boosts (boost_combat/intellect/agility) and stat-replacement 'use willpower instead' (Ceremonial Sickle/Dowsing Rod/Onyx Pentacle -> BuffStatsReplace/StatsModBoost); test-initiation with difficulty (Bonesaw, Alchemical Distillation -> TestInitiate*); damage-plus (DamagePlus); uses pools + replenish + discard-when-zero (UsesStarting/Support, DiscardZeroUses) for charges/supplies/secrets/evidence/aether/keys/time; cost structures (fast/free/reaction discard-self/exhaust-self/spend-resource, CostActionMultiple); succeed/fail-by margins (SkillValueSucceedBy*/TestResult); clue discovery + additional clues + shroud reduction (ClueDiscover*, ClueAdditional*, LocationShroud*, compound clue-tech); card draw and resource gain economy (DeckDrawYou/Investigator, GainResource*); search top-N (DeckSearch* with range — covers Prepared for the Worst top-9, Captivating Discovery top-6, Friends in Low Places top-6, Kicking the Hornet's Nest encounter top-9); healing (Heal* incl. ally/investigator + compound support); elite-unusable (EnemyEliteNonEliteOnly); attach asset/enemy/location (Attach*); recursion of events/assets/skills incl. play-from-discard (Salvage, Uncage the Soul, Improvised Shield -> Recursion* / DiscardPile*); chaos-token cancel-and-redraw (Custom Modifications, Analysis -> ChaosRevealAnotherInstead); auto-success / auto-evade testless (Exploit Weakness, Existential Riddle, String of Curses -> Auto*/TestlessEvade); deck restriction and trait-support tags. IMPORTANTLY VERIFIED NOT A GAP: 'play another card from hand/discard reducing its cost' (Motivational Speech, Ever Vigilant, 'I'll take that!', Uncage the Soul, Chuck Fergus) IS already covered by TagCostDiscount (amount arg) — confirmed against its canonical use on 01686 Old Book of Lore ('play that card, reducing its cost by 2'). GENUINE GAPS proposed above: (1) commit to ANOTHER investigator's test / commit at a distance — no existing tag, only the framework timing point TimingSkillSt2CommitCards; (2) accumulating renamed-token engine (evidence/leads/offering placed from the token pool onto self) — distinct from printed Uses pools; (3) draw-extra-encounter-and-choose-which-to-resolve (Dr. Maleson, Nature of the Beast) — distinct from full CancelEncounterDraw. RECOMMEND ARG EXTENSIONS rather than new tags: add target (self | chosen-investigator) to TagActionAdditional to capture the strong extra-action archetype (Guidance/Press Pass/End of the Road/Lifeline). AMBIGUITIES I COULD NOT FULLY RESOLVE: (a) whether 'customizable' deserves a game-effect tag — it is pervasive here (Hunter's Armor, Runic Axe, Raven Quill, Grizzled, etc.) but appears to be card metadata handled outside this effect taxonomy, so I did not propose it; (b) damage-redirection/soak onto an asset ('may be assigned damage/horror dealt to other investigators at your location' — Obsidian Bracelet 09024, Girish Kadakia 09038) is a recurring tank mechanic with no existing tag, but only 2-3 cards here and I was unsure whether the project intends to tag damage-assignment redirection — flagging for synthesis rather than proposing; (c) several attach-to-enemy lockdown sub-effects (exhaust-on-move, 'cannot take damage this round', 'doom cannot be placed on it', 'gains aloof') are individually untagged but may be considered too granular.

args.name: from
args.type: SkillType (the stat whose value is added, e.g. agility)

proposedTags.rationale: Multiple cards add a SECOND stat's value on top of the test's base stat, e.g. Lockpicks (60305) 'Add your [agility] value to your skill value for this investigation', Cheap Shot (60312) 'Add your [agility] value to your skill value for this attack', Slip Away (60314) 'Add your [intellect] to your skill value for this evasion attempt'. This is NOT a flat numeric boost (StatsModBoostInTest has a fixed value) and NOT a passive from/to swap (BuffStatsReplace). It is a recurring Rogue 'double-stat' mechanic players search for. No existing tag expresses 'add the value of stat X into this test'.

Stat-substitution for a specific action is a signature Rogue effect with no tag. Pilfer (60315) 'This investigation uses [agility] instead of [intellect]', Backstab (60329) 'This attack uses [agility] instead of [combat]', Sharpshooter (60327) 'This attack uses [agility] instead of [combat]'. The old hints split this into stat_use_agility + stat_not_intellect, but the searchable concept is the single substitution. BuffStatsReplace (from/to) is documented as a passive stat-replacement buff on a card, not a per-action 'use X instead of Y for this test' override; the digest's example usage and the action-scoped nature here justify a distinct test-scoped tag.

args.name: target
args.type: 'self' | 'other-asset' (whether it readies itself or another asset)

proposedTags.rationale: Readying an exhausted asset (refunding its exhaust cost) has no tag in the taxonomy at all — the only 'ready' references in the digest are the upkeep phase step and EnemyDoesNotReady. Mauser C96 (60306) 'either ready Mauser C96 or gain 1 resource', Beretta M1918 (60331) 'either ready Beretta M1918, or this attack deals an additional +1 damage'. This is a recurring weapon-tempo archetype (ready-on-success) that deckbuilders search for.

Several Rogue events return THEMSELVES to hand instead of discarding, enabling reuse. Cheap Shot (60323) 'return Cheap Shot to your hand at the end of your turn', Backstab (60329) 'return Backstab to your hand at the end of your turn', Pilfer (60328) 'return Pilfer to your hand', Slip Away (60324) 'return Slip Away to your hand'. The existing recursion/* tags (RecursionAsset/Event/Skill) describe pulling OTHER cards from discard; PlayAreaToHand is for assets bouncing to hand. A self-returning event is a distinct, very searchable value-engine mechanic with no current tag.

Opportunist (60319) 'If you succeed by 3 or more, return Opportunist to your hand after this test instead of discarding it.' A committed skill card returning to hand instead of being discarded is a recurring Rogue skill-recursion mechanic distinct from returning from play (events) and not covered by any recursion or play-area tag.

args.name: source
args.type: 'own-deck' | 'investigator-discard' (where the committed card is fetched from)

proposedTags.rationale: Cards that dig for a skill card and force-commit it mid-test have no tag. Daredevil (60318) 'discard cards from the top of your deck until you discard a [rogue] skill you can commit to this test. Commit it.' Copycat (60330) 'search the discard pile of another investigator for a skill you can commit to this test, and commit it.' This is search/commit synergy (skill-icon tech) the deckbuilder searches for; DeckSearch/DeckDiscard tags describe the digging but not the auto-commit of a fetched skill, and TimingSkillSt2CommitCards is only a timing point.

proposedCompoundTags.conceptDescription: Cards that let an investigator perform a test or action with a different/secondary stat than the one normally used — either substituting (use X instead of Y) or adding a second stat's value to the test. The hallmark 'flex stat' Rogue/Survivor archetype players deckbuild around (e.g. fight with agility).
proposedCompoundTags.rationale: Pilfer/Backstab/Sharpshooter substitute the action's stat while Lockpicks/Cheap Shot/Slip Away add a second stat; players searching for 'use my best stat for everything' want both grouped. Both members are newly proposed and share the broader 'stat flexibility' archetype.

proposedCompoundTags.conceptDescription: Cards that recover themselves or other cards for repeated use — self-returning events/skills (return to hand/deck instead of discarding) plus the existing recursion-of-other-cards tags. The value-engine archetype players search to build sustainable card advantage.
proposedCompoundTags.rationale: This Rogue pack centers on reusable events (Cheap Shot, Backstab, Pilfer, Slip Away all bounce back) and a reusable skill (Opportunist). Grouping the proposed self-recursion tags with existing recursion tags surfaces the whole 'reusable card' archetype across packs.

archetypes.name: Succeed-by reward (overkill payoff)
archetypes.description: Nearly every card in this pack rewards EXCEEDING the difficulty by a margin (succeed by 1/2/3/4), unlocking bonus damage, evade, card draw, readying, or self-return. Defines the Winifred/Rogue 'big swing' identity. Already well-served by existing SkillValueSucceedByOrMore/Exactly and the succeed-by compound tag, but the density here flags it as the pack's core theme.

archetypes.name: Flex-stat / stat-substitution toolkit
archetypes.description: Rogue cards that let you apply agility (or another off-stat) to actions that normally use a different stat, either by substitution or addition. A cross-pack archetype (Rogue/Survivor) that lets a one-good-stat investigator do everything.

archetypes.name: Reusable event engine (return-to-hand)
archetypes.description: Tactic/Trick events that return themselves to hand on a strong success instead of being discarded, plus Opportunist's committed-skill return. A signature Rogue card-economy archetype.

archetypes.name: Weapon ready-on-success (firearm tempo)
archetypes.description: Firearm assets that ready themselves (refunding their exhaust) when the attack succeeds by a margin, letting a single weapon attack multiple times per turn. Recurring across Guardian/Rogue firearm lines.

coverageNotes:
Pack 'win' is the Winifred Habbamock (Rogue) starter/upgrade set: 27 cards, dominated by skill-test 'succeed-by-margin' payoffs. The EXISTING taxonomy already covers most of it well: succeed-by/fail-by margins (SkillValue* + compound succeed-by), action initiation (ActionBold* for Fight/Evade/Investigate), flat in-test stat boosts (StatsModBoostInTest*, e.g. Mauser +2 combat), passive boosts (Lonnie +1 combat = StatsModBoostPassive), spend-resource-for-boost (Streetwise = StatsModPumpResource + CostFreeSpendResource — fully covered, no gap), uses/ammo (UsesStarting/Support), costs (cost-action/fast/free/reaction exhaust/spend), card draw (DeckDraw*), the Lucky Cigarette Case search-top-X (DeckSearchYou with range top + shuffle), healing (Heal* for Lonnie/Liquid Courage), auto-evade (AutoEvade for Cheap Shot), enemy-does-not-ready (Slip Away), gain-resource (Sneak By/Mauser), discount/fast-granting (Chuck Fergus = CostDiscount + fast), trait support (TraitSupport* firearm/tactic/trick), deck restriction, testless self-move (Nimble = LocationMoveInvestigatorSelf), commit timing, and result conditions (SkillTestConditionSuccessful/Fail). The GENUINE GAPS, all recurring beyond this pack, are: (1) add-a-stat's-value-to-the-test (Lockpicks/Cheap Shot/Slip Away/Pilfer) — distinct from a flat numeric boost; (2) use-stat-X-instead-of-Y per action (Pilfer/Backstab/Sharpshooter) — BuffStatsReplace is documented as a passive card buff, not an action-scoped test override; (3) ready an asset (Mauser/Beretta) — no 'ready' tag exists at all; (4) self-recursion of events/skills returning to hand from play or commit (Cheap Shot/Backstab/Pilfer/Slip Away/Opportunist) — existing recursion tags cover pulling OTHER cards, and PlayAreaToHand is asset-specific; (5) fetch-and-commit a skill card mid-test from deck or another investigator's discard (Daredevil/Copycat). AMBIGUITIES: (a) Whether the proposed stat-substitution tag should reuse/extend BuffStatsReplace via an optional 'action' arg rather than be a new tag — I propose a new tag because the digest frames BuffStatsReplace as a passive replacement of one stat by another card-wide, whereas these are one-shot per-action test overrides; a maintainer may prefer adding an optional 'action'/'scope' arg to BuffStatsReplace instead. (b) Sharpshooter's second mode 'Use the attacked enemy's evade value for this attack instead of their fight value' is enemy-stat substitution already partially expressible via EnemyValueEvade/EnemyValueFight presence, but there is no explicit 'use enemy's evade-in-place-of-fight' substitution tag — left unflagged as a separate proposal since it is a single card here, but note it as a future micro-gap.</coverageNotes>
